items.title: Full list of African countries where cars are made
items.description: By Hannah Ogunlabi Africa’s automotive industry is often associated with the assembly of cars belonging to international brands, but several African countries have also developed their own vehicle brands and manufacturing operations. From Nigeria’s Innoson and Nord Automobiles to Ghana’s Kantanka, Uganda’s Kiira Motors and Morocco’s Laraki, these companies have developed vehicles ranging from passenger cars and SUVs to buses, pickups and sports cars. While their production volumes vary considerably, they represent some of the continent’s efforts to develop indigenous automotive manufacturing. Here are 10 African automobile manufacturers and vehicle brands to know. 1. Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing – Nigeria Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing (IVM) is a Nigerian automobile manufacturer based in Nnewi, Anambra State. The company produces a range of vehicles, including passenger cars, SUVs, buses, pickup trucks and other commercial vehicles. IVM has promoted its vehicles as being designed and produced for African markets and conditions. The company is one of the best-known examples of indigenous automobile manufacturing in Nigeria and has expanded its range to include several locally branded models. 2. Nord Automobiles – Nigeria Nord Automobiles is another Nigerian vehicle manufacturer with a growing range of locally branded vehicles. The Lagos-based company describes its vehicles as “truly made in Nigeria” and currently lists models including the Nord A3, A5, A7, A9, C3, Demir, Max, Tusk, Tank and Tripper. Its 2026 range includes SUVs, sedans and utility vehicles, with the company also promoting locally built hybrid technology. 3. Kantanka Automobile – Ghana Kantanka Automobile is a Ghanaian vehicle manufacturer founded by Apostle Kwadwo Safo. The company has developed and produced vehicles under its own Kantanka brand, including SUVs, saloon cars and utility vehicles. Kantanka is one of Ghana’s most prominent indigenous automotive brands and has become a symbol of the country’s efforts to increase local participation in vehicle manufacturing. 4. Kiira Motors Corporation – Uganda Kiira Motors Corporation (KMC) is a Ugandan state-backed vehicle manufacturer focused on developing vehicles for African markets. The company is particularly known for its work on electric and environmentally friendly transportation. Its projects include the Kiira EV and Kayoola range of electric buses and other vehicles. KMC’s development forms part of Uganda’s efforts to build a domestic automotive industry while promoting cleaner forms of transportation. 5. El Nasr Automotive Manufacturing Company – Egypt El Nasr Automotive Manufacturing Company is Egypt’s state-owned automobile manufacturer and one of the country’s longest-established vehicle companies. Founded in 1960, the company has returned to active production after a prolonged period of limited operations. In May 2026, El Nasr announced the production of its 1,000th locally manufactured passenger vehicle. The company also produces buses and minibuses and has entered partnerships aimed at expanding locally manufactured vehicles. In June 2026, El Nasr signed a strategic agreement with China’s FAW Group to produce a range of vehicles under the Nasr brand. 6. Laraki – Morocco Laraki is a Moroccan luxury and performance-car manufacturer founded by designer and entrepreneur Abdeslam Laraki. Unlike mass-market manufacturers, Laraki has focused on limited-production, high-performance vehicles. Its best-known projects include the Fulgura, Borac and Epitome. The company has attracted international attention for developing exotic sports cars from Morocco and remains one of Africa’s most distinctive indigenous automotive brands. 7. Wallyscar – Tunisia Wallyscar is a Tunisian automobile manufacturer established in the 2000s. The company has developed compact and lightweight vehicles, with models including the Izis and Iris. Wallyscar has been associated with producing practical vehicles for African and other markets. It is among the African brands that have attempted to develop vehicles under a locally owned marque rather than simply assembling an international brand. 8. Birkin Cars – South Africa Birkin Cars is a South African sports-car manufacturer known for lightweight roadsters inspired by the Lotus Seven concept. Its Birkin S3 is a notable model associated with the company and has been produced for performance enthusiasts in South Africa and overseas. Birkin represents a different side of Africa’s automotive industry, focusing on low-volume sports cars rather than mass-market passenger vehicles. 9. SNVI – Algeria Société Nationale des Véhicules Industriels (SNVI) is an Algerian manufacturer specialising primarily in commercial and industrial vehicles. Its production has included trucks, buses, coaches and other heavy-duty vehicles used in transportation and industrial applications. Unlike manufacturers on this list that focus heavily on passenger cars, SNVI’s importance lies mainly in Algeria’s commercial-vehicle manufacturing sector. 10. Proforce – Nigeria Proforce is a Nigerian company involved in the production of specialised vehicles and mobility solutions. The company is particularly associated with armoured and security vehicles rather than conventional passenger cars. Its inclusion highlights the wider scope of Africa’s indigenous automotive industry, which extends beyond family cars and SUVs to specialised vehicles. Nigeria’s indigenous automotive sector therefore includes several manufacturers working across different vehicle categories, including Innoson, Nord Automobiles and Proforce. items.title: Houet : Le FC Triple Alliance remporte le tournoi du FACS à Satiri
items.description: Houet : Le FC Triple Alliance remporte le tournoi du FACS à Satiri Satiri, 2 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le FC Triple Alliance a remporté, le lundi 31 août 2026 à Satiri, la première édition du tournoi de football du Festival artistique et culturel de Satiri (FACS), en battant le FC Soukoro Jr 5 tirs au but à 4, après un score nul de 0-0 au terme du temps réglementaire. La compétition, placée sous le signe de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble, a été initiée par la jeunesse locale. La finale s’est disputée sur le terrain de l’école primaire A de Satiri, en présence d’un public nombreux venu encourager les deux équipes. Vêtus respectivement de bleu et d’orange, les joueurs du FC Triple Alliance et du FC Soukoro Jr ont livré une rencontre engagée, sans parvenir à se départager au terme du temps réglementaire. La décision s’est finalement jouée aux tirs au but. Plus adroit dans cet exercice, le FC Triple Alliance s’est imposé 5 tirs au but à 4, décrochant ainsi le trophée de cette première édition. Le représentant du chef de terre, Lassina Balla Traoré, a salué la mobilisation de la jeunesse et la tenue de cette compétition, estimant que le sport constitue un important facteur de rapprochement entre les populations. « Le football peut rassembler les jeunes, renforcer la cohésion sociale et favoriser le vivre-ensemble », a-t-il déclaré, invitant les habitants à conjuguer leurs efforts pour contribuer au développement de la commune de Satiri. Le président du comité d’organisation, Lassina Traoré, a, pour sa part, exprimé sa reconnaissance aux équipes participantes, aux supporters et à toutes les personnes ayant contribué à la réussite de la compétition. Au terme de la finale, le FC Triple Alliance a reçu le trophée de vainqueur ainsi qu’une enveloppe financière, tandis que le FC Soukoro Jr, finaliste malheureux, a été récompensé d’une enveloppe financière. Cette première édition du tournoi s’inscrit dans le cadre des activités du FACS, une initiative de la jeunesse de Satiri visant à promouvoir le sport et la culture, tout en renforçant la cohésion sociale et le vivre-ensemble au sein de la commune. items.title: Pakistan, Kyrgyzstan sign agreement to boost bilateral trade to $200m in two years
items.description: Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost their bilateral trade to $200 million in two years. The agreement was signed in Bishkek before Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and his delegation wound up their three-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. Addressing the signing ceremony, PM Shehbaz said the two sides had initially signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to expand their bilateral trade to $200m. But, he continued, “I suggested that an agreement should be signed instead of an MoU as it would be a concrete step to achieve [the target of] $200m trade.” The prime minister said he requested Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to consider this possibility and he agreed. Subsequently, an agreement was signed at the airport, he added. Earlier in the day, the PM addressed a joint briefing alongside the Kyrgyz president, where he had announced the plan to expand bilateral trade between the two countries. “To this end, we will be working on a comprehensive plan of practical measures aimed at gradually increasing bilateral trade to $200 million, improving trade mechanisms, promoting joint investment projects, strengthening industrial cooperation and expanding direct business-to-business contacts,” he said after the two countries signed multiple memoranda (MoU) of understanding. He said he had noted during their meeting prior to the briefing that currently, bilateral trade between Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan stood at around $16 million, which, he said, was “not a patch on our friendship and our very strong relations.” He recalled that during his talks with President Zhaparov, he had noted that “our present-day bilateral trade stands at around $16m, which is not a patch on our friendship and our very strong relations”. “Today, we should have signed not an MoU but an agreement to make sure that in the next two years we increase our bilateral trade from $16m to $200m per annum. And this is not a very difficult task. Let us convert this MoU straight away into an agreement, if you kindly agree, after this meeting,” he added. He said the two had held talks focused on economic cooperation and agreed that “our economic partnership must now move to a more practical and result-oriented stage”. The prime minister further stated, “We welcome greater engagement between Pakistani businesses and financial institutions and their Kyrgyz counterparts to carry forward our shared vision of enhancing our bilateral economic cooperation.” PM Shehbaz said connectivity remained central to the two countries’ shared vision of closer economic integration between South and Central Asia. “We welcome the signing of the agreement on transit trade, which will help facilitate trade, improve logistics and create new opportunities for regional connectivity,” he added. He said the two sides had also reaffirmed the importance of effectively implementing the quadrilateral agreement on traffic and transit and agreed to work towards simplifying transport, customs and administrative procedures. “Energy cooperation is another very important pillar of our partnership,” he said, adding that the two sides had reaffirmed the importance of timely implementation of the Casa-1000 project and welcomed the establishment of a joint working group on energy to develop practical cooperation in the areas of electricity, hydropower, renewable energy, energy infrastructure and modern technologies. “I am pleased that our two sides have expanded cooperation in education, science and technology, health, culture and tourism,” he further stated. “We warmly welcomed the establishment of sister-city ties between Osh and Lahore,” he said, describing them as two ancient cities whose iconic landmarks reflected their rich history and cultural heritage. PM Shehbaz said security and defence cooperation had also featured prominently in their discussions. The two sides reaffirmed their resolve to strengthen cooperation in the fight against terrorism, extremism and other contemporary threats, he added. The two leaders also discussed regional and international issues of mutual concern, in addition to bilateral matters, PM Shehbaz said. The prime minister said the two sides had agreed to deepen cooperation on environmental issues and concurred that effective multilateralism was key to resolving the priority issues of the day and achieving global peace and security. “We remain committed to working together at the UN and other multilateral fora,” he said. “Pakistan regards the Kyrgyz Republic as its most important and valued partner in Central Asia, and we mean it.” He told President Zhaparov he hoped that his visit marked the beginning of many more such interactions between the two countries. PM Shehbaz also invited President Zhaparov to visit Pakistan at a mutually convenient time. Earlier in his address, he thanked the Kyrgyz president and the government and people of Kyrgyzstan for a “warm welcome and generous hospitality extended to me and my delegation”. He further congratulated the people of Kyrgyzstan on behalf of the people of Pakistan on their independence day. PM Shehbaz also extended felicitations to Kyrgyzstan for hosting the sixth World Nomad Games, on its election as a non-permanent of the United Nations Security Council for 2027-28 and on its successful chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2025–2026. “We are also very happy that Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and his team worked tirelessly for your election as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council,” he said, adding that it was “heartening to witness Kyrgyzstan’s remarkable progress and development under your (President Zhaparov) energetic leadership”. He added that Kyrgyzstan had also made “impressive economic gains and taken meaningful steps to translate this progress into an improved quality of life through expanded public services and targeted support for vulnerable communities”, “I fully share your commitment to deepening cooperation between our two countries and strengthening the bonds between our two peoples in pursuit of our shared interests and broader goals of peace and cooperation among nations. “And in this regard, I commend the positive and constructive spirit of our discussions held today, which culminated in the signing of several MoUs aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation and economic exchanges for the mutual benefit of our countries and our peoples,” he said. The Kyrgyz president also spoke alongside PM Shehbaz at a ceremony, delivering his remarks in Kyrgyz. According to a translation carried by state-run Radio Pakistan , he said that “at a time when international tensions are increasing, strengthening friendship, deepening mutual understanding and developing cooperation are more important than ever”. He said the joint statement signed after their talks reflected a shared vision for further strengthening Kyrgyz-Pakistani relations and identified key areas of cooperation. Zhaparov said the economy should be “one of the main pillars” of the bilateral partnership and that the two countries had agreed to take steps to boost bilateral trade, expand the range of traded goods and attract investment. The Kyrgyz president further stated that the two sides were ready to undertake joint projects in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, energy, light industry, tourism, the digital economy, virtual assets and other fields. Zhaparov said Pakistan’s seaports offered Kyrgyzstan a natural route to South Asian markets and global trade routes. He said the two countries had traditionally maintained close cooperation at the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and the Economic Cooperation Organisation. He also congratulated Pakistan on assuming the chairmanship of the SCO. Both leaders signed a joint statement encompassing the discussions and goals of Prime Minister Shehbaz’s visit to Bishkek. The Foreign Office (FO) later issued a joint statement by the two countries, which added that the two leaders also condemned terrorist attacks in the region and beyond and “stressed the significance of stability, safety and security in Afghanistan as an important condition for realising the vision of seamless connectivity between South Asia and Central Asia”. “In this regard, both leaders reiterated that Afghan territory should not be used for activities that pose threats to the security of other countries, in accordance with its international obligations,” it added. The two sides agreed that a secure and conducive environment was necessary to realise the enormous potential for cooperation and connectivity between South Asia and Central Asia. The statement further said the Pakistani side “reaffirmed its support for international initiatives of the Kyrgyz Republic aimed at advancing the global mountain agenda, sustainable development of mountain regions and adaptation to climate change, including the holding of the Second Mountain Summit Bishkek +25 in 2027”. MoUs signed Earlier, PM Shehbaz and President Zhaparov witnessed the ceremony where the representatives from both sides exchanged the pre-signed documents. The two sides signed a diplomatic Programme of Cooperation between their foreign ministries for 2026-27 besides an MoU between the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad and the National Institute for Strategic Initiatives of the Kyrgyz Republic to strengthen research collaboration. Both countries also finalised agreements on transit trade to facilitate bilateral commercial movement and promote science and technological cooperation, besides signing a treaty on extradition, the APP report said. The governments of both countries formulated a draft agreement on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, and an MoU was signed between the interior ministries of Pakistan and Kyrgyz Republic to combat the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, precursor chemicals, and related issues. The Kyrgyz health ministry and Pakistan Medical and Dental Council signed an MoU focused on cooperation in medical education while another MoU was signed between the education ministries of both countries to promote cooperation in the field of education. The Kyrgyz Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology and Technical Supervision and Pakistan’s Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination signed an MoU to strengthen cooperation in the field of environment and climate change. Moreover, Pakistan, National Defence University and the National Institute for Strategic Initiatives of the Kyrgyz Republic signed an MoU for academic research and cooperative activities. The National Agency for Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies under the Kyrgyz President and the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority signed an MoU for cooperation in virtual assets. Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan also signed an agreement on the establishment of a sister city relationship between Lahore and Osh city of Kyrgyzstan. Furthermore, OJSC Kyrgyz Post and Pakistan Post reached a bilateral agreement for mutually beneficial cooperation in postal services and e-commerce while another agreement was signed between the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the Kyrgyz Republic and the Federation of Pakistan Chamber of Commerce and Industry on cooperation to boost bilateral business ties. Pakistan and the Kyrgyz Republic also signed multiple bilateral accords to enhance cooperation in security, education, environment and technology sectors. PM’s arrival at presidential palace PM Shehbaz had reached Bishkek on Monday, primarily to attend a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit that concluded on Tuesday. He visited the presidential palace, Yntymak Ordo, today for his engagement with the Kyrgyz president and was given red-carpet welcome and a guard of honour upon his arrival, a statement by Pakistan’s government said. “He was warmly received by President Zhaparov [and] the national anthems of Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan were played as the two leaders stood at the salute dais. “The smartly-turned out contingents of the Kyrgyz armed forces presented the guard of honour,” the statement detailed. Both leaders introduced their respective delegations to each other before proceeding for their meeting, it added. According to the statement, PM Shehbaz later visited the Ata Beyit Memorial Complex in Bishkek, where he was received by Kyrgyzstan’s First Deputy Prime Minister Daniar Amangeldiev and Minister of Culture, Information and Youth Mirbek Mambetaliyev. The prime minister laid a wreath at the grave of renowned Kyrgyz writer Chingiz Aitmatov and offered Fateha, it added. Later, the prime minister also visited Ala Archa National Park in Bishkek, accompanied by President Zhaparo, the statement said. During the visit, a demonstration of Kyrgyz culture and traditional activities, including cultural dances and other traditional arts, was presented to the prime minister, it added. Describing Kyrgyzstan’s cultural traditions as admirable, PM Shehbaz emphasised the importance of further strengthening the historical, cultural and fraternal ties between the peoples of the two countries, according to the statement.

items.title: The Air Marshals Keeping Watch On Eric Swalwell
items.description: O n August 8 , former Representative Eric Swalwell boarded a United Airlines flight from Frankfurt, Germany, to Washington, D.C. He didn’t know it, but federal agents were watching him throughout the nine-hour trip. The FBI had asked the Federal Air Marshal Service to covertly monitor Swalwell on board and to watch him use his electronic devices, to see whether its officers could visually ascertain his passcodes, according to records I obtained that have not previously been reported on. Air marshals are trained to blend in with other passengers and quietly keep tabs on their subjects, who are usually suspected terrorists or potential hijackers, not politicians. But Swalwell is an enemy of sorts to the Trump administration. For years, the Democrat has been one of Donald Trump’s most visible political antagonists, having served as a manager in the president’s second impeachment trial. Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller has called Swalwell a “scumbag” on national television. And FBI Director Kash Patel, the leader of the agency that wanted Swalwell monitored, described him as one of the “corrupt actors of the first order” in his 2023 book, Government Gangsters . The directive for air-marshal surveillance said that Swalwell was the “focus” of an FBI investigation, but it didn’t provide additional details. Law enforcement has good reason to investigate the 45-year-old. This past spring, a former staff member accused Swalwell of twice raping her while she was intoxicated. A woman in California accused Swalwell of drugging and raping her after he’d promised to assist with her career. Three more women have accused Swalwell of making unwanted advances and sending them lewd text messages, including nude pictures of himself. Swalwell has denied the allegations, but authorities in Los Angeles and Manhattan have opened a criminal investigation. In April, as the number of accusers mounted, Swalwell suspended his campaign for governor of California and resigned from his seat in Congress. A week after the flight from Germany, Swalwell got off another plane at San Francisco International Airport. FBI agents were waiting for him with a search warrant. They seized his mobile phone and personal computer. (It’s not clear whether, by that point, the FBI knew the passcodes to unlock those devices.) The next day, agents searched Swalwell’s home in Washington, D.C. Documents filed in federal court in California suggest that the bureau is investigating Swalwell in connection with the sexual-assault cases in Los Angeles and New York. Despite the seriousness of the accusations against Swalwell, many aspects of the FBI’s request to the Federal Air Marshal Service were unusual, current and former officials told me. For one thing, the FBI does not usually investigate sexual assault. For another, asking air marshals to obtain a subject’s electronic passcodes is considered out of the ordinary even for traditional subjects of surveillance, one former official said. The agency presumes that requests for assistance from the FBI, which are not unusual, are relevant to a legitimate investigation. But the bureau’s behavior here undermines that confidence, the former official added. The request to monitor Swalwell was classified as “Special Mission Coverage,” a term for ad hoc requests from law-enforcement or intelligence agencies that don’t involve people on security watch lists. The FBI’s decision to ask air marshals for help also puzzled some former law-enforcement officials I spoke with, who asked why the FBI hadn’t put its own agents on the plane to conduct surveillance, which would have been a routine matter. Given the public evidence and the history of the Trump administration’s efforts to investigate or discredit Swalwell, current and former officials and security experts told me that they have trouble imagining that the federal government would have gone to such lengths if the accused were not one of the administration’s least favorite people. They spoke on the condition of anonymity because they didn’t want to provoke reprisals. Sara Azari, Swalwell’s lawyer, told me in a statement that Swalwell has been in contact with the Department of Justice throughout the assault investigation. “Not once were we asked for Mr. Swalwell’s phones or devices. Had the DOJ asked, we would have complied, as we have with every other request,” she said. Azari called the air-marshal surveillance an “extraordinary escalation” against her client, who has not been charged with a crime. The FBI declined to comment. The Transportation Security Administration, which runs the air-marshals service, didn’t respond to emails and phone calls requesting comment. T he midair surveillance of the former lawmaker is not the only unusual step the federal government has taken in this case. The warrant used to seize Swalwell’s electronic devices cited a civil-rights statute that historically has been applied to police officers who abuse their authority while acting “under color of law.” It traces its origins to the 19th century and was used in the 1960s to charge local police in Mississippi who conspired with Klansmen to murder civil-rights workers. Decades later, two of the police officers who’d beaten Rodney King were convicted under the law. And it was used to bring federal charges against Derek Chauvin, the officer convicted in Minnesota of killing George Floyd. The FBI hasn’t publicly articulated its rationale for applying the law to Swalwell. But one theory, according to legal experts I spoke with, may be that he used the power of his office to intimidate his alleged victims into silence. Prosecutors might believe that there’s evidence of coercion or threats in Swalwell’s electronic communications. But it’s not clear that the law would apply to a legislator as it does to law-enforcement officials, who have the power to detain people. “Mr. Swalwell’s private relationships between consenting adults have nothing to do with his office, his authority, or his official duties,” his lawyer said. The fact that details about the search of Swalwell’s devices and home are publicly known is also a departure from usual law-enforcement procedure. The inventory of what the agents took from him at the San Francisco airport, which should have been kept under seal, was somehow made public. Under Patel, the FBI has publicized its investigative steps against high-profile suspects before they have been charged. In August 2025, Patel posted on X about an imminent FBI action just as agents began raiding the home of former National Security Adviser John Bolton , a Trump critic. Broadcasting a secret operation in advance could tip off a suspect and potentially put agents in physical danger. At least one news organization appeared to have known ahead of time about the Bolton raid. A month later, Patel posted that “the subject” in the murder of Charlie Kirk was in custody, hours before it was true. He also posted details about leads that agents were following in the Kirk case, which could have jeopardized the investigation. [ Read: The FBI director is MIA ] It’s possible that the FBI is interested in Swalwell for reasons that go beyond his alleged treatment of women. The Department of Homeland Security is investigating his employment of a nanny from Brazil. Swalwell is also among the Trump critics whom Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte criminally referred to the Department of Justice over alleged mortgage fraud. Swalwell has never been charged, however, and experts have pointed out that Pulte’s allegations against officials probably reflect paperwork errors, not genuine attempts to defraud lenders. Swalwell was also once a subject in a counterintelligence investigation of a suspected agent for China’s intelligence service. But in 2017, the FBI cleared him, and the Justice Department didn’t file charges. A former U.S. official familiar with the case told me that the representative had cooperated with investigators after they’d presented him with evidence that the woman he knew might be a foreign operative. Last month, the administration made the unusual decision to publicly release classified FBI files related to that investigation. Swalwell’s conservative critics have long been obsessed with the case of Christine Fang, known as Fang Fang, who the files show was suspected of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. The files helped the public understand more details about Chinese espionage. But they also revealed that Swalwell had admitted to having a physical relationship with Fang. Embarrassing Swalwell might have been the point of disclosing the documents. Patel has made no secret of his contempt for Swalwell. During a House Judiciary Committee hearing last September, when Swalwell was a member, they sparred over whether Trump’s name appeared in files from the investigation of Jeffrey Epstein, and what Patel had told then–Attorney General Pam Bondi about the matter. Swalwell accused Patel of being evasive and showing “consciousness of guilt.” Swalwell then cited Patel’s book, in which Swalwell’s name appears on a list of “deep state” actors. Twenty of those people, Swalwell said, had already been investigated or faced “adverse actions.” He asked whether Patel would recuse himself from any investigations of the people he had named, including Swalwell. “I’m going to borrow your terminology and call bullshit on your entire career in Congress. It has been a disgrace to the American people,” Patel said. The two men spoke over each other. Finally, the FBI director answered Swalwell’s question. “No,” he said, he would not recuse. Madison Hahamy and Marie-Rose Sheinerman contributed research to this story. *Illustration Sources: Tierney L. Cross / Bloomberg / Getty; Tom Williams / CQ-Roll Call, Inc / Getty.

items.title: Yeumbeul : quatre individus poursuivis pour harcèlement sexuel et transmission présumée du VIH
items.description: Le Commissariat d’arrondissement de Yeumbeul Comico a procédé au déferrement au parquet de quatre individus poursuivis pour plusieurs faits présumés, notamment association de malfaiteurs, harcèlement sexuel, acte contre nature, transmission volontaire du VIH et mise en danger de la vie d’autrui. L’affaire a débuté dans la nuit du 29 août 2026, vers 00 h 29. De retour d’une mission d’intervention, les éléments de la Brigade de recherches ont conduit au commissariat un individu soupçonné de harcèlement sexuel. Selon les éléments de l’enquête, son interpellation faisait suite à la plainte d’un homme qui aurait reçu des avances à caractère sexuel après que le mis en cause eut obtenu son numéro de téléphone en se présentant comme un client intéressé par ses services. Entendu sur les faits, le suspect aurait reconnu les faits qui lui étaient reprochés. Son placement en garde à vue et les investigations menées par les enquêteurs auraient ensuite permis d’identifier plusieurs personnes avec lesquelles il aurait été en contact. Les investigations ont également porté sur l’exploitation des téléphones portables saisis. Les enquêteurs indiquent avoir découvert, notamment sur WhatsApp et Messenger, des échanges qu’ils présentent comme faisant état de relations intimes entre les personnes concernées. Par ailleurs, des réquisitions sérologiques adressées au Centre de santé de Keur Massar auraient révélé que deux des mis en cause sont séropositifs au VIH. À l’issue de l’enquête, les quatre individus ont été maintenus en garde à vue avant d’être conduits au parquet. Ils sont poursuivis pour association de malfaiteurs, harcèlement sexuel, acte contre nature, transmission volontaire du VIH et mise en danger de la vie d’autrui. Ces faits demeurent, à ce stade, des accusations et les mis en cause bénéficient de la présomption d’innocence jusqu’à une éventuelle décision de justice.

items.title: Banwa : 37 acteurs de l’éducation renforcent leurs capacités en éducation bi-plurilingue à Sanaba
items.description: Burkina-Bankui-Éducation-Formation Banwa : 37 acteurs de l’éducation renforcent leurs capacités en éducation bi-plurilingue à Sanaba Sanaba, 2 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Trente-sept acteurs de l’éducation de la Circonscription d’éducation de base (CEB) de Sanaba prennent part, du 1er au 14 septembre 2026, à une session de formation consacrée à la transcription et à la didactique des disciplines dans le cadre de l’éducation bi-plurilingue. La cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de la session a été présidée le mardi 1er septembre 2026 à l’école Sanaba « A » par le Chef de la CEB de Sanaba, Jean Konaté. La formation regroupe 18 enseignants titulaires de classes de Cours préparatoire première année (CP1) et 19 directeurs d’écoles de la CEB de Sanaba. Durant quatorze jours, les participants seront outillés notamment sur la transcription en langue dioula, les démarches didactiques des différentes disciplines ainsi que l’élaboration de fiches pédagogiques. Selon les organisateurs, cette session vise à renforcer les capacités des acteurs chargés de la mise en œuvre de la formule harmonisée d’éducation bi-plurilingue afin de leur permettre d’en assurer une meilleure application et une bonne maîtrise de la transcription. En donnant le top départ de la formation, le Chef de la CEB de Sanaba, Jean Konaté a invité les participants à suivre avec assiduité les différents enseignements dispensés, afin de pouvoir les réinvestir efficacement auprès des apprenants. À l’issue de la cérémonie d’ouverture, le Directeur provincial de l’Éducation préscolaire, primaire et non formelle des Banwa Pedro Blaise Coulibaly a rendu visite aux participants. Il est venu les encourager et leur témoigner son soutien dans le cadre de cette session de renforcement des capacités. Agence d’information du Burkina LRS/SO/wis

items.title: Messi departure leaves Argentina facing rebuild after golden era
items.description: Argentina face a testing transition period as they attempt to move on from Lionel Messi’s international retirement, with question marks also hanging over the futures of coach Lionel Scaloni and several ageing players. Messi vacated the famous number 10 shirt on Monday, after 21 years of carrying Argentinian hopes on his shoulders. It was a burden that weighed heavily initially, before a golden era late in his career during which the South American giants won three major titles, including the 2022 World Cup. The 39-year-old’s last competitive match for Argentina was the 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final in July. Of the 17 players who featured in that match for Scaloni’s side, only two will be under the age of 30 when the next World Cup kicks off in South America in 2030. Veteran centre-back Nicolas Otamendi, 38, retired from international duty in the wake of the loss to Spain in New Jersey, when Argentina were thoroughly outplayed by younger, more vibrant opponents. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has since suggested he may follow suit, as has 32-year-old midfield enforcer Leandro Paredes, who was slapped with a 10-match ban by FIFA for attacking Spain players after the final whistle. “If he (Messi) isn’t there, it will be hard for everything to keep working the way it used to,” Paredes told Argentinian TV channel TN. Rodrigo De Paul’s international career has also been heavily linked with his Inter Miami teammate’s. The biggest question marks surround the future of coach Scaloni, who has overseen the most successful spell for the Albiceleste since the days of Diego Maradona. The 48-year-old, whose team are known as the “Scaloneta” at home, was appointed in 2018 and ended Argentina’s 28-year wait for a major trophy with victory in the 2021 Copa America. The former Deportivo La Coruna right-back’s current deal runs out in December. Scaloni had reportedly agreed a contract extension until 2030 before the World Cup, but he cast doubt on his future after the poor performance in the final. “I already have an idea of what I want to do,” Scaloni said after the loss. “I’m going to honour my contract, and then we’ll see. I need to think, because I don’t know if it’s possible to achieve something as great as this.” The next World Cup will be largely held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, but Argentina will be one of three South American nations hosting one match, thus gaining automatic qualification. First, though, they will be targeting a third consecutive Copa America crown in 2028. Despite Messi’s retirement, there will likely still be plenty of familiar faces in a squad who will remain title favourites. Lisandro Martinez and Cristian Romero have established themselves as the first-choice centre-half pairing. Enzo Fernandez, who moved to Manchester City from Chelsea on Monday for a fee that equalled the British transfer record, and Alexis Mac Allister have made the central midfield positions their own, while Messi’s departure could give Inter Milan’s Lautaro Martinez and Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez more space to shine up front. Alvarez in particular will be expected to improve significantly on his ratio of 15 goals in 59 caps. – ‘Great young players’ – Messi himself believes the long-term future is bright for his country. “I’ve given it my all. I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” he said when announcing his retirement. Exciting Como youngster Nico Paz made two appearances at the World Cup and could become a more regular starter, while 23-year-old Giuliano Simeone — son of former Argentina stalwart Diego Simeone — impressed as a substitute in the semi-final win over England. Real Madrid winger Franco Mastantuono did not make the World Cup squad but has already won four international caps at the age of 19. Argentina’s next generation impressed at last year’s Under-20 World Cup in Chile, reaching the final for the first time since 2007 before losing to Morocco. Argentina currently have no fixtures scheduled for the international break later this month but the Argentinian football association is reportedly planning a possible farewell match for Messi, the country’s record goalscorer and record appearance maker with 125 goals in 207 games. He leaves a huge hole — but a new generation will endeavour to fill it. The post Messi departure leaves Argentina facing rebuild after golden era appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Former Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Dr Mustapha Hamid, has emerged as the leading candidate in the race for the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) First Vice Chairman position, according to a poll by Global InfoAnalytics. Dr Hamid secured 18.3% of voter preferences, narrowly ahead of Henry Nana Boakye and Nana Akomea, who each polled 17.5%. The poll places Kojo Fosu Boaudu in fourth position with 5.6%, followed by Masawudu Osman with 4.5% and Richard Ahiagbah with 3.8%. Yaa A. Frimpong recorded 3.1%, while Abena Pokuaa Amoah polled 1.4%. Samuel Yeyune and Abankwa Yeboah each secured 1.3%. Other candidates, including Horma Miezah (0.7%), Bright Essilfie Kumi (0.1%) and Richard Oti Aboagye (0.0%), recorded comparatively lower levels of support. However, the poll also shows a significant level of uncertainty, with 19.7% of respondents undecided. The findings come ahead of the NPP’s national executive elections scheduled for October, where members of the party will elect new national officers. The figures suggest a closely contested race among the leading candidates, with Dr Hamid holding only a slight margin over Nana Boakye and Nana Akomea.

items.title: Taliban govt defends ban on protest, citing Islamic law
items.description: The Taliban government defended on Wednesday its ban on protests that has drawn condemnation from rights groups, saying the order complies with Islamic law. Demonstrations in Afghanistan have been rare since the Taliban returned to power just over five years ago, but the government last month introduced a rule holding that “all types of protests are banned”. International organisations have decried the law as “ruthless” and a move to suppress any dissent in the country. Taliban government spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid told AFP during a news conference that the “law fully complies with Islamic law”, adding that “protests don’t exist in Islamic law”. “Protests belong to societies where there are different laws established, for example a democracy or a republic,” Mujahid said. Under the Islamic system, he said, people can approach the government with concerns rather than hold demonstrations. Mujahid argued the ban “will also protect people from wasting time” and prevent the destruction of private property. Human Rights Watch late last month slammed the ban as “another step in the Taliban’s ruthless effort to suppress all dissent”. Amnesty International described the Taliban’s broader series of changes to law enforcement as “another sweeping assault on human rights in Afghanistan”, calling the protest ban “among its most egregious provisions”. While demonstrations are rare, at least two people were killed in June when security forces reportedly opened fire on a women’s rights protest in the western city of Herat, a group of UN experts said. items.title: Burkina Faso : L’équipe de l’administration pénitentiaire remporte la 8e édition de la Coupe du directeur général
items.description: La finale de la 8e édition du tournoi de maracana féminin de la résilience, dénommée la Coupe du directeur général de l'administration pénitentiaire, a eu lieu ce 1er septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Elle a été remportée par l'équipe de l'administration pénitentiaire aux tirs au but face à l'équipe du Groupement central des armées. L'équipe victorieuse de la coupe du directeur général de l'administration pénitentiaire a remporté la somme de 500 000 FCFA en plus du trophée et des médailles. La deuxième équipe, le Groupement central des armées, a reçu une enveloppe de 400 000 FCFA et des médailles. Les joueuses de la Gendarmerie nationale, troisièmes de la compétition, ont reçu la somme de 300 000 FCFA et des médailles. « C'est la première fois vraiment (de remporter la finale de la coupe, NDLR). On est très contentes, on est dépassées. Pour la première fois depuis la première édition. Voilà, on n'a jamais été en finale. C'est la toute première fois comme ça. Avant tout, on est contentes. On a vraiment rehaussé l'image du corps », a précisé Clémence Ouédraogo, capitaine de l'équipe victorieuse. La 8e édition de la compétition a été placée sous le thème : « corps en mouvement, esprit en paix : le sport comme levier de guérison et de cohésion au sein des FDS ». Selon le promoteur, l’Inspecteur Divisionnaire Sabila Sawadogo, directeur général de l'administration pénitentiaire, le niveau de jeu des équipes était élevé. Les équipes féminines, composées de FDS et de VDP ont démontré un savoir-faire en alliant travail et jeu. Aussi, il a indiqué que l'objectif était de renforcer la cohésion entre les différents corps des Forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que les VDP. l’Inspecteur Divisionnaire Sabila Sawadogo,directeur général de l'administration pénitentiaire©️Faso7 « Avec ce tournoi féminin de résilience, nous remarquons que le Burkina Faso grandit, nous sommes résilients et c'est ça pour montrer que le Burkina Faso avance », a-t-il ajouté. Le représentant du ministre de la Justice a aussi rappelé l'importance du sport pour les FDS. Il a souligné qu'il constitue une thérapie pour ces derniers qui sont régulièrement confrontés à la pression du théâtre des opérations et à l'impact émotionnel et psychologique qu'elle génère. Le plus important, dit-il, le sport permet de réduire les barrières entre la hiérarchie militaire et les subordonnés. « Ce tournoi incarne la résilience des populations burkinabè qui choisissent la vie, la dignité et la fraternité. Il met en lumière l'engagement exemplaire des femmes FDS qui nous offrent une double leçon de courage : celle de la combattante et celle de la citoyenne. Mais le sport est aussi un levier de cohésion. Sur le terrain, les distinctions hiérarchiques s'effacent. Ce qui demeure, c'est l'équipe, l'effort collectif, la solidarité, la discipline et la fraternité d'armes », a-t-il indiqué. La 8e Coupe du directeur général de l'administration pénitentiaire a été placée sous les parrainages d'Ida Ouédraogo/Paré, directrice générale du Fonds d'appui au sport et à la presse privée (Wassa Bondo) et du Lieutenant Colonel Adama Sawadogo, président de l'Office de liaison de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (OLAO). Selon eux, cette compétition témoigne de la résistance du pays face à l'adversité. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : L'équipe de l'administration pénitentiaire remporte la 8e édition de la Coupe du directeur général est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Boubacar Yacine Diallo porté à la tête de la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée : cap sur la jeunesse, la formation et les réseaux sociaux
items.description: Élu le 1er septembre 2026 à la tête de la Plateforme des Régulateurs de l'Audiovisuel des pays membres de l'UEMOA et de la Guinée (PRA-UEMOA-Guinée) lors de sa 12ᵉ Assemblée générale à Conakry, le président de la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC) de Guinée, Boubacar Yacine Diallo, succède au Togolais Pitalounani Telou pour un mandat de deux ans. ​Pour mener à bien sa mission, le nouveau président entend placer les compétences sous-régionales et la jeunesse au centre de ses priorités. ​« Que cette presse soit félicitée, qu'elle soit encouragée ! Et qu'elle sache que la dynamique d'assainissement que la HAC a entreprise n'est pas dirigée contre la presse, au contraire : c'est pour assainir les rangs des journalistes (…) pour que les journalistes et la profession soient respectés (…) Je voudrais donc rassurer la presse que ce mandat de 2 ans lui est dédié (…) la relève est parfaitement assurée, j'en suis convaincu », a-t-il déclaré . ​Sur le plan financier et opérationnel, Boubacar Yacine Diallo prône une utilisation pragmatique des ressources au service de la profession : ​ « Il va falloir utiliser cet argent-là (…) il ne devra pas dormir, il doit servir à quelque chose (…) Mais je pense qu'il y a des priorités, et pour moi, la première priorité, c'est le renforcement des capacités des journalistes. » ​Face aux défis contemporains du paysage médiatique, il appelle à un partage d'expériences en matière de régulation des médias numériques : ​« L'expérience de la Guinée a prouvé que nous n'avons pas besoin d'aller chercher des compétences en dehors de notre continent (…) Et je suis sûr, en tout cas pour nous qui sommes en retard, par exemple dans le domaine de la régulation des réseaux sociaux, très rapidement nous allons solliciter les pays qui sont en avance pour que nous puissions être en mesure de réguler sans censurer les réseaux sociaux (…) qui sont à la fois utiles et nuisibles selon l'usage que les auteurs en font. » 0 ​Principales recommandations de l'Assemblée Générale ​L'événement, qui a réuni les instances de régulation de neuf pays (Togo, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Sénégal, Guinée-Bissau, Côte d'Ivoire, Bénin et Tchad), s'est conclu par la lecture de plusieurs orientations stratégiques lues par Matar Sall (CNRA du Sénégal) : ​Pour les États : Adapter les cadres législatifs pour étendre les compétences de régulation aux plateformes numériques, aux plateformes de partage et à l'intelligence artificielle. ​Pour la PRA-UEMOA-Guinée : ​● Promouvoir l'éducation aux médias et harmoniser les réglementations pour faire face aux contenus transversaux; ● ​Mettre en œuvre l'accord de collaboration avec l'UEMOA pour adopter des normes communautaires et négocier directement avec les plateformes numériques (transparence des algorithmes et modération); ​● Solliciter l'UEMOA pour inviter la Guinée-Bissau à garantir l'indépendance et l'autonomie financière de son Conseil National de la Communication Sociale. ● ​Assurer la régularité des travaux du Comité des juristes experts en TIC. Il est important de rappeler que l'événement a réuni les dirigeants des instances de régulation de huit pays membres de l’UEMOA aux côtés de la Guinée. Il s'agit du Togo, du Burkina Faso, du Mali, le du Niger, du Sénégal, de la Guinée-Bissau, de la Côte d'Ivoire et du Bénin. Le Tchad a également marqué sa présence.

Koulsé/Montée des couleurs: les appelés à IPO appelés à assurer la relève de l’administration
items.description: BURKINA-KOULSE-MONTÉE-COULEURS-NATIONALES Koulsé/Montée des couleurs: les appelés à IPO appelés à assurer la relève de l’administration Kaya, 1er sept. 2026 (AIB) – Les appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO), nouvellement sortis de leur formation, ont participé mardi à Kaya à la montée mensuelle des couleurs nationales aux côtés des corps constitués de la région des Koulsé. Cette initiative vise à les familiariser avec les institutions dont ils constituent la future relève. La cérémonie, organisée à la Direction régionale de l’Office national de l’eau et de l’assainissement (ONEA), a réuni les autorités administratives, les responsables des services déconcentrés, les acteurs de la société civile, les Forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que les jeunes appelés. Dans son message du mois, la gouverneure par intérim de la région des Koulsé, Bernadette Adenyo/Sermé a indiqué que la présence des appelés IPO à cette cérémonie solennelle devait leur permettre de s’imprégner de l’organisation et du fonctionnement des différents corps constitués, selon « Si nous avons souhaité que les AIPO soient des nôtres, c’est pour faire aussi une immersion pour eux en ce qui concerne l’organisation des corps constitués », a-t-elle expliqué. L’autorité régionale a présenté ces jeunes comme la future relève des responsables et acteurs actuellement engagés dans le fonctionnement de l’administration et la construction de la Patrie. « Vous êtes nos petits frères, vous êtes nos enfants, et vous êtes la relève qui succédera à chacun de nous », leur a-t-elle lancé. Camarade Adenyo/Sermé a invité les AIPO à conserver les enseignements reçus durant leur formation et à les traduire dans leur comportement quotidien. « Nous voulons continuer de voir des citoyens réellement transformés qui impactent leur génération et qui sont des modèles dans leur famille, dans leur communauté et pour cette nation, le Burkina Faso », a-t-elle insisté. La gouverneure par intérim a enfin exhorté les jeunes appelés à poursuivre leurs études avec engagement afin de pouvoir, demain, intégrer l’administration et les différents secteurs d’activité et contribuer à la construction du Burkina Faso. Agence d’Information du Burkina MJO/aio/bak

items.title: Standard Chartered Bank pays GH¢97.8m dividend to SSNIT
items.description: Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC has paid GH¢97.8 million in dividends to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) for the 2025 financial year, strengthening returns from the pension manager’s investment portfolio. The payment forms part of the bank’s total dividend distribution of GH¢673.95 million following shareholder approval at its 56th Annual General Meeting in Accra. The bank declared a final dividend of GH¢4.98 per ordinary share, amounting to GH¢672.35 million, alongside a GH¢1.13 million preference share dividend. For SSNIT, the payment provides additional liquidity to support its pension obligations while delivering a cash return from one of its listed equity investments. Chief Executive Officer of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana PLC, Xorse Godzi, said SSNIT remains an important stakeholder because of its position as a shareholder and its role in Ghana’s economy. He said the bank’s relationship with SSNIT reflects the wider connection between its operations and Ghanaian workers, who have an indirect stake in the institution through the pension fund manager. “We recognise that SSNIT plays a vital role in Ghana’s economy, representing financial security for the future of the average worker. Through SSNIT, the average Ghanaian worker has a stake in our Bank. Our success, therefore, directly contributes to the future of Ghanaian workers,” Mr. Godzi said The dividends payment comes as Standard Chartered marks 130 years of continuous operations in Ghana. Its local history dates to the establishment of the Bank of British West Africa in 1896, with the bank currently focused on cross-border banking, wealth management, trade and infrastructure financing. Director-General of SSNIT, Kwesi Afreh Biney, said improving investment returns remains a core part of the trust’s strategy, making dividend-generating holdings important to the sustainability of its investment portfolio. He said Standard Chartered had delivered both capital appreciation through its listed shares and direct cash returns through dividends, providing funds that can be deployed toward pension payments. “You have not only given us enhanced returns on our investments in the SSNIT portfolio, but you have also introduced an improvement that provides us with greater liquidity to support the payment of pensions which is the core of our job and mandate,” the Director General said. Mr. Biney described Standard Chartered as one of SSNIT’s important investments and among the stronger dividend-paying companies on the Ghana Stock Exchange.

items.title: Incident de Leipzig : Paris convoque le chargé d’affaires russe, Moscou dénonce une fiction accusatoire
items.description: La France convoque a nouveau le charge d'affaires par interim de la Russie pour « protester tres vivement ». Cette fois-ci, la convocation fait suite aux accusations portees par Berlin a l'encontre de Moscou concernant l'incident impliquant un drone charge d'explosifs a l'aeroport de Leipzig, survenu debut août dernier. « Comme a chaque fois, nous n'allons pas detourner les yeux et nous allons marquer notre desapprobation et notre condamnation en tirant les consequences de tels actes », a declare le 2 septembre le ministre francais des Affaires etrangeres, Jean-Noel Barrot, cite par BFMTV. Il s'est egalement dit convaincu que l'analyse de l'incident menee par Berlin demontrerait « la volonte de saboter cet avion et ce site logistique qui a ete utilise pour aider l'Ukraine ». Outre le charge d'affaires par interim de la Russie en France, le representant permanent par interim de la Russie aupres de l'Union europeenne a egalement ete convoque a la suite de cet incident, a indique la chef de la diplomatie europeenne, Kaja Kallas. Elle a egalement ajoute qu'outre la convocation des ambassadeurs, les etats membres de l'UE discuteraient des mesures supplementaires qu'ils pourraient prendre. Incident a Leipzig : une escalade fondee sur un pretexte invente Dans la soiree du 4 août, un employe de l'aeroport de Leipzig aurait repere, a proximite d'un avion-cargo ukrainien, un drone qui transportait, selon lui, environ 800 g d'explosifs. L'Allemagne a declare qu'elle tenait la Russie pour responsable de l'incident, mais l'ambassade de Russie en Allemagne l'a qualifie de « provocation montee a la hâte » et a affirme que cet episode servait les interets de Kiev et des partisans d'une militarisation accrue de l'Europe, tout en alimentant, en Allemagne, un climat anti-russe ainsi que les appels a une confrontation accrue avec Moscou. Malgre l'absence de toute preuve, Berlin a profite de cet incident pour annoncer de nouvelles mesures de durcissement a l'egard de la Russie, notamment la fermeture du consulat general russe a Bonn a compter du 18 septembre et la resiliation de l'accord autorisant l'exploitation de la Maison russe dans la capitale. De plus, l'Allemagne a approuve un renforcement des controles a l'entree sur son territoire pour les citoyens russes. Maria Zakharova, porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, a fermement rejete les accusations de Berlin, soulignant que les autorites allemandes avaient une nouvelle fois choisi l'escalade dans les relations bilaterales, en s'appuyant sur un « pretexte totalement invente » . « Aucun element de preuve convaincant et serieux n'a ete presente », a-t-elle declare, ajoutant que Moscou repondrait a « toutes les decisions antirusses » prises par Berlin. Le president russe Vladimir Poutine a quant a lui attribue cette decision des autorites allemandes aux difficultes actuelles que connaît l'Allemagne, et plus precisement a la position delicate du chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz, qui ne jouit pas de la confiance de ses concitoyens, car il ne defend pas les interets nationaux de l'Allemagne, mais les « brade ». Il a egalement evoque les difficultes de l'economie allemande, citant les fermetures d'entreprises, les pertes d'emplois et la baisse du niveau de vie.

items.title: LGA commends State-Owned Enterprises for recording strong 2025 performance
items.description: The Legal Green Association (LGA) has commended the government, the State Interests and Governance Authority (SIGA), and the boards and management of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) for what it describes as significant improvements in the performance of the state-owned sector in the 2025 financial year. According to the LGA, in a statement signed by Festus Matey, Leader of the LGA, and Evans Mawunyo Tsikata, Head of Politics and Elections, the improvements, as reported in the 2025 State Ownership Report released by SIGA, indicate progress in public-sector performance, financial management and institutional efficiency. The report shows that SOEs recorded a consolidated net profit after tax of GH¢19.80 billion in 2025, compared with a net loss of GH¢2.25 billion in 2024. Total SOE revenue also increased by 28.12 per cent, from GH¢137.64 billion in 2024 to GH¢176.43 billion in 2025. The LGA said it welcomed reported growth in agriculture, manufacturing and infrastructure, as well as reductions in finance costs and public-sector procurement infractions and improved foreign exchange performance. It also noted the growth of joint venture companies (JVCs) and commended SIGA for strengthening oversight, performance monitoring and corporate governance across the state-owned sector. The association, however, said the reported improvements should translate into greater benefits for Ghanaians, particularly through the creation of sustainable jobs. It cited Article 36(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which directs the state to manage the national economy in a manner that maximises economic development and provides adequate means of livelihood and suitable employment. The LGA said profitable and strategically positioned state enterprises should expand production, establish new investment lines, support local value chains and create sustainable employment opportunities, particularly for the youth. While welcoming the increase in employment across specified entities, which brought the workforce to 98,724, the association said the number of sustainable jobs created should become an important measure of the success of the government’s economic reset agenda. It said the focus should shift from recovery to resilience, compliance to performance, public expenditure to public value, and state ownership to sustainable value creation. The LGA further urged SIGA to continue its performance assessments and take appropriate lawful measures against entities that consistently fail to meet their statutory and commercial obligations. It expressed concern about continued losses and negative equity reported by some state entities, and called for interventions such as restructuring, recapitalisation, strategic partnerships, mergers or, where legally justified and in the public interest, liquidation. Such interventions, it said, must comply with the Constitution, relevant legislation, principles of natural justice and applicable public financial management and corporate governance requirements. The association also called for profitable state enterprises to reinvest strategically in productive capacity, technology, infrastructure and employment-generating activities. It urged government and SIGA to ensure that the gains recorded in 2025 become permanent structural improvements rather than a temporary rebound.

items.title: Raja : Paco Jémez dévoile ses ambitions et promet de faire évoluer les Verts
items.description: Le Raja de Casablanca a officiellement présenté son nouvel entraîneur, l’Espagnol Paco Jémez, qui succède à Nasreddine Nabi. Le technicien de 54 ans entend rapidement imprimer sa marque, tout en appelant à la patience pour construire une équipe capable de répondre aux ambitions du club. Le Raja Club Athletic a présenté mardi soir son nouvel entraîneur, Paco Jémez, lors d’une conférence de presse organisée à l’académie du club. Le technicien espagnol prend les commandes de l’équipe première après la fin de l’aventure de Nasreddine Nabi sur le banc des Verts. Dès ses premiers mots, Jémez a affiché sa satisfaction de rejoindre le Raja, tout en mesurant l’importance de la mission qui l’attend. Pour lui, entraîner un club de cette dimension représente une responsabilité particulière et nécessite de travailler sur plusieurs aspects. « J’ai déjà commencé le travail avec l’équipe et j’envisage de changer certaines choses et de développer le mental des joueurs pour pouvoir réaliser les objectifs fixés » , a expliqué le nouvel entraîneur. Le technicien espagnol a toutefois insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas brûler les étapes. La construction d’une équipe compétitive demande, selon lui, du temps, du travail et une véritable progression collective. « Nous travaillons sans relâche et les conditions sont réunies » , a-t-il assuré, tout en reconnaissant que bâtir une équipe forte ne peut pas se faire du jour au lendemain. Ziyat défend un projet à long terme Présent lors de cette conférence de presse, le président du Raja, Jawad Ziyat, a de son côté voulu inscrire l’arrivée de Jémez dans une vision plus large de la restructuration du club. Le dirigeant a expliqué que l’activation de la société sportive du Raja vise à renforcer les structures du club et à poser les bases d’un modèle capable de produire des résultats durables à moyen et long terme. Dans cette nouvelle organisation, le poste de directeur sportif occupe une place centrale. Ziyat a ainsi rappelé que le Raja a confié de larges prérogatives au Portugais Rogério Matias, chargé notamment de participer à la construction de l’effectif et au choix de l’entraîneur. Le président a également précisé que le conseil d’administration de la société sportive et le comité sportif assurent le suivi et l’orientation du projet. Trois semaines pour imposer sa philosophie Rogério Matias, qui s’exprimait publiquement pour la première fois depuis sa nomination en juillet, s’est dit particulièrement fier de travailler pour le Raja, qu’il a qualifié de « plus grand club en Afrique » en raison notamment de sa popularité. Le directeur sportif a appelé l’ensemble des composantes du club à travailler avec détermination afin de répondre aux attentes élevées des supporters. De son côté, Jawad Ziyat a indiqué que Paco Jémez disposait d’environ trois semaines pour commencer à mettre en place son style de jeu et façonner une équipe à son image. Une période qui s’annonce donc décisive pour le technicien espagnol, appelé à rapidement trouver ses repères et à transmettre ses principes à son groupe. Un technicien habitué au football espagnol Paco Jémez arrive au Raja avec une solide expérience du banc. Au cours de sa carrière, il a notamment dirigé Cordoue, Las Palmas, le Rayo Vallecano, Grenade et Ibiza. Son parcours lui a permis d’évoluer à plusieurs niveaux du football espagnol et de développer une philosophie basée sur le jeu et la personnalité collective. Sa dernière expérience remonte à West Ham United, où il occupait le poste d’entraîneur adjoint jusqu’à l’hiver dernier. Après cette expérience en Angleterre, Jémez ouvre donc un nouveau chapitre de sa carrière au Maroc avec un défi de taille : remettre le Raja sur une trajectoire ambitieuse et répondre aux attentes particulièrement élevées de son public. Son arrivée intervient quelques jours après la séparation entre le Raja et Nasreddine Nabi. Le club avait annoncé la fin des fonctions du technicien tunisien, précisant que la décision avait été prise dans le respect des dispositions contractuelles liant les deux parties. Avec Paco Jémez, le Raja mise désormais sur une nouvelle philosophie et une organisation sportive renforcée. Reste à savoir si le technicien espagnol parviendra rapidement à transformer cette nouvelle dynamique en résultats sur le terrain. items.title: The million-dollar problem sitting offshore: Why Ghana’s cement makers are adding GH¢12 to every bag
items.description: There is trouble brewing ofshore, and Ghana’s cement manufacturers want to make sure the public understands the operational realities driving their latest pricing decision. Sources close to the sector say manufacturers are preparing to introduce a “Clinker Demurrage Surcharge” of around GH¢12 per bag. The move follows months of escalating, unbudgeted operational losses tied to severe congestion at Tema Port. The industry estimates these costs have reached a shocking US$45 to US$50 million this year alone. The core issue stems from extended waiting times at anchorage. Clinker, the key raw material required for cement production, took around seven days to clear port at the beginning of the year. That wait has since ballooned to 40 days. To make matters worse, daily vessel demurrage rates have risen to approximately US$27,000 per day. A single vessel sitting idle for 40 days racks up over US$1 million in penalty fees before offloading a single tonne. The challenge is more than just financial. With clinker taking 35 days to travel from China and another 35 to 40 days waiting at Tema, the supply cycle is stretching toward three months. That extended lead time creates a structural bottleneck if port congestion persists. So who pays? The industry emphasizes that the upcoming GH¢12 addition is not a standard price increase. Instead, it is being structured as a temporary, direct pass-through surcharge, itemized separately on invoices and subject to quarterly review. If port clearance times normalize, the surcharge can be adjusted downwards or removed completely. Beyond the GH¢12 adjustment, industry stakeholders are appealing for broader inter-agency collaboration to resolve the port bottleneck. The substantial demurrage fees currently being incurred represent a significant drain on foreign exchange, capital flowing directly to international ship owners lines instead of circulating within the Ghanaian economy. Manufacturers acknowledge ongoing discussions with key government stakeholders, including the Ministries of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry and Transport, but emphasize that port infrastructure and berthing availability remain severely constrained. Industry players point to potential relief solutions, such as optimizing access to Berths 10 and 11, which could immediately help clear the vessel backlog. The core message from Ghana’s cement makers is collaborative: addressing port congestion will eliminate the demurrage burden and the need for the surcharge. Until those port operations are streamlined, however, the industry faces the financial reality of passing on the cost of prolonged offshore delays.

items.title: Real Madrid’s Asencio convicted of drink-driving
items.description: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio was convicted of drink-driving in Gran Canaria in August, a court source confirmed to AFP on Wednesday. The 23-year-old centre-back was more than three times over the legal limit and fined 14,400 euros ($16.7k), while his driving licence was suspended for eight months. Asencio was convicted in a trial held in San Bartolome de Tirajana, a village in Gran Canaria, after the incident on August 16. Asencio, who is from the Canary Islands, was not with Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid squad at the time because he was still recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered at the end of July. This week, Asencio is due to face another court case in Gran Canaria, involving the alleged non-consensual sharing of a sexual video dating back to 2023. Spanish media report Asencio expects to be cleared in that case if the two women who were filmed formally forgive him. Three former Real Madrid reserve players are also on trial for allegedly recording and distributing the video. The trial is scheduled for September 3, 4 and 7. items.title: Aviation militaire : 42 millions de dollars pour renforcer la formation des pilotes de F-16
items.description: L’aviation militaire marocaine va se doter de deux nouveaux systèmes complets de simulation pour ses F-16 Block 72. Le groupe canadien CAE a décroché un contrat pouvant atteindre 42,1 millions de dollars, incluant également un volet de soutien logistique, dans le cadre du programme américain de ventes militaires à l’étranger. La montée en puissance de la flotte marocaine de F-16 s’accompagne désormais d’un renforcement des capacités de formation. Selon les informations publiées par le Département américain de la Défense dans son bulletin quotidien des contrats, le groupe canadien CAE a obtenu un marché destiné à fournir à l’aviation militaire marocaine deux systèmes de simulation complets pour les F-16 Block 72, ainsi qu’un ensemble de prestations de soutien logistique. Le contrat peut atteindre 42,1 millions de dollars. Près de 38 millions de dollars ont été engagés dès son attribution dans le cadre du mécanisme américain des Foreign Military Sales (FMS), par lequel les États-Unis organisent les ventes d’équipements militaires à leurs partenaires étrangers. Les travaux seront réalisés à Arlington, au Texas, ainsi qu’à la base aérienne de Sidi Slimane. Leur achèvement est prévu au plus tard le 30 avril 2029. Deux simulateurs pour une flotte en pleine modernisation Les équipements commandés correspondent à deux systèmes de simulation de mission complète. Leur vocation est de reproduire, dans un environnement virtuel, les conditions d’utilisation opérationnelle d’un F-16 Block 72. Chaque dispositif comprend notamment un cockpit reproduisant celui de l’appareil, des postes destinés aux instructeurs et aux opérateurs, un système de visualisation, des capacités de calcul et de traitement informatique, un dispositif de distribution électrique ainsi qu’un système de visée monté sur casque. L’ensemble comprend également un serveur central, une alimentation électrique sécurisée et des équipements de maintenance et de soutien. Pour l’aviation militaire, l’intérêt de ce type d’installation dépasse la seule formation initiale des pilotes. Les simulateurs permettent de préparer des missions, de reproduire des situations opérationnelles complexes et de multiplier les heures d’entraînement sans mobiliser systématiquement les avions. Cette solution permet ainsi de réduire les coûts associés aux heures de vol réelles, tout en limitant l’usure des appareils et en offrant la possibilité de répéter des scénarios difficiles ou rares dans un environnement contrôlé. Une coopération déjà engagée avec CAE Ce nouveau contrat ne marque toutefois pas le début de la relation entre le Maroc et CAE dans le domaine de la formation sur F-16. Le Royaume figure déjà parmi les programmes actifs du groupe canadien consacrés à l’entraînement sur cet avion de combat. Le nouveau marché s’inscrit donc davantage dans une extension des capacités existantes que dans le lancement d’une coopération entièrement nouvelle. Le programme intervient surtout à un moment où l’aviation militaire marocaine poursuit une transformation importante de sa flotte de chasse. Le Maroc a commandé 24 nouveaux F-16V, également désignés sous le nom de « Viper », correspondant à la version la plus récente de l’appareil. Parallèlement, les F-16 déjà en service doivent être modernisés afin de rejoindre ce nouveau standard. Le développement des moyens de simulation apparaît ainsi comme l’un des volets nécessaires à cette évolution. L’arrivée d’appareils plus modernes, dotés de systèmes électroniques et de capacités de mission plus avancés, implique en effet une adaptation parallèle des infrastructures de formation et de préparation opérationnelle. Sidi Slimane, un site au passé stratégique Le choix de la base aérienne de Sidi Slimane présente également une dimension historique. Connue comme la cinquième base aérienne de l’aviation militaire marocaine, elle a été initialement construite en 1951 comme base de l’US Strategic Air Command. Durant la guerre froide, le site avait notamment accueilli des unités américaines équipées de bombardiers B-47. Les forces américaines se sont ensuite retirées de la base, qui a été transférée sous contrôle marocain en 1963. Plus de six décennies plus tard, Sidi Slimane s’apprête donc à accueillir de nouvelles infrastructures directement liées à la modernisation de la flotte marocaine de F-16. La formation, un maillon de la modernisation L’investissement dans la simulation illustre une dimension moins visible, mais essentielle, de la modernisation des forces aériennes : la capacité à former et à maintenir au plus haut niveau les équipages appelés à exploiter les nouveaux systèmes. L’acquisition d’un avion de combat moderne ne se limite pas à la livraison de la plateforme. Elle suppose également la mise en place d’un environnement complet associant formation, maintenance, soutien logistique et infrastructures techniques. Le contrat attribué à CAE s’inscrit précisément dans cette logique. Alors que la flotte de F-16 est appelée à évoluer vers le standard Viper, le développement des capacités de simulation permettra d'accompagner cette transition par un entraînement plus régulier et davantage centré sur les systèmes de mission des appareils. En novembre dernier, Northrop Grumman avait également obtenu un contrat de 303,6 millions de dollars pour assurer des services de réparation et de soutien des radars de F-16 au profit de huit pays, dont le Maroc, seul pays africain concerné par ce programme de ventes militaires américaines.
