items.title: E-challans for littering in Lahore markets
items.description: LAHORE: The Suthra Punjab Authority (SPA) on Tuesday launched an e-challan system to penalise littering at public places in Lahore, whereas burning tyres and waste will be dealt very strictly with fines up to Rs500,000 with imprisonment. “It is a pilot project limited to the Lahore metropolitan city’s 200 commercial markets and major roads, including The Mall, Jail Road and Ferozepur Road. Initially, the 25 teams have started the e-challan service from Tuesday by issuing warnings to those involved in littering,” Lahore Suthra Punjab Authority CEO Shehryar Arif Khan said while talking to Dawn. “The total enforcement staff deputed for the e-challan system consists of as many as 75 people, including 50 divided in two field and supervising teams,” he added. According to him, the month of September would be treated as a grace period for the violators who would be formally fined with effect from October 1 onwards. To a question, he said that the e-challan system in residential areas was currently not under consideration as the authority’s teams would first educate the people. “I cannot say until when we will start penalising the people littering in residential areas,” he added. He said that while issuing warnings in commercial areas and model roads, the teams, during the grace period, would also tell them that they committed a crime which shouldn’t be repeated. Meanwhile, the e-challan system was formally launched at a ceremony at Liberty Chowk attended by Lahore Deputy Commissioner retired Capt Ali Ejaz and Shehryar Arif Khan. Briefing the media, the officials said that anti-littering squads had been deployed across the city’s roads, markets and commercial centres to monitor violations and raise public awareness about cleanliness laws. Under the new system, warnings and awareness messages were being issued from Tuesday and violators would be issued warning e-challans starting Sept 1, 2026, without any fines. Officials said the initial focus would be on educating citizens rather than immediately imposing penalties. However, repeated violations of cleanliness regulations would result in legal action and fines. According to the officials, people found throwing or burning waste on roads would face heavy fines under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2025 and the Suthra Punjab Authority Act, 2026. A fine ranging from Rs1,000 to Rs10,000 would be imposed for littering in public places, while failure to maintain cleanliness outside a house, shop or factory could attract a fine of Rs1,000 to Rs50,000. Shops and shopping malls found using prohibited plastic bags will be fined between Rs1,000 and Rs2,000 respectively. The officials said that burning waste could result in a fine ranging from Rs100,000 to Rs500,000 and imprisonment for up to two years. Burning tyres, whether by an industrial unit or an individual, may attract a fine of up to Rs500,000 and imprisonment for up to seven years. All fines would have to be paid through banking or digital channels with officials barred from accepting cash payments. “The anti-littering squads have been deployed with the objective of making Lahore a waste-free city. The squads will also educate citizens about the safe disposal and transfer of waste and inform them about the applicable cleanliness laws,” Mr Shehryar said. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

items.title: Salir de Ceuta por su propio pie: “No puedo más, me voy. Aún no sé para qué vine”
items.description: Tarek y su hermana Salma llegan mirando al suelo y arrastrando los pies. Vinieron a Ceuta sin nada y se van sin nada por la frontera. Ni una lágrima ni una mirada atrás cuando salen de Ceuta. Ambos describen el último mes como “el peor” de sus vidas. Sin embargo, ampliando la mirada, su aventura ha roto una ciudad, se enmarca en una crisis con ramificaciones internacionales , con Rusia, Israel e Italia en el punto de mira, y ha puesto al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez frente a su mayor emergencia migratoria. “No puedo más, me voy. Aún no sé para qué vine”, dice Tarek, de 20 años, antes de abandonar Ceuta hacia Marruecos por un camino de tierra —el único habilitado para quienes entraron de forma ilegal y deciden regresar— a un costado del control de pasaportes. “Quiero volver al instituto”, añade su hermana Salma, de 17 años, que decidió unirse a la caravana para entrar en España sin saber muy bien por qué. Tarek y Salma han pasado un mes juntos protegiéndose mutuamente y emprenden este lunes su regreso a Oued Laou, a dos horas en coche de Ceuta y a cinco de Melilla por la costa. Seguir leyendo

Publicada en los países de lengua alemana en septiembre de 2025, la novela superó los 200.000 ejemplares y vendió sus derechos de traducción a una treintena de territorios. Patti Smith la elogió en público y Dua Lipa la recomendó a sus seguidores, mientras que Tom Tykwer, director de Corre, Lola, corre y de la serie Babylon Berlin, ya prepara su adaptación al cine. items.description: El voraz aumento de los abonos con tarjeta ha conseguido que los pagos con monedas o billetes supongan ya solo el 57% de las compras. Según datos del Banco de España correspondientes al segundo semestre de 2025 y difundidos el pasado julio, las operaciones con tarjeta aumentaron respecto al año anterior un 11,4%, con 13.009 millones en un año. El importe de estas operaciones alcanzó los 219.000 millones de euros, un 10,9% más que en el segundo semestre de 2024. Sumándole la primera mitad de 2025 (195.000 millones), llegamos a 414.000 millones de euros abonados con plástico en un año. Las cantidades medias de cada pago se van reduciendo (de 31,9 euros a 31,6), y eso significa que millones de personas abonan ya con tarjeta diariamente la barra de pan, el litro de leche o las chuches para las criaturas. items.description: Óscar López entra en su oficina directo desde el aeropuerto. Lleva un traje azul y una corbata que se quitará dentro de un rato en un gesto de alivio y de fin de día. En el avión que le traía desde Santander no ha escuchado la entrevista que Pedro Sánchez le ha dado esta mañana a la Cadena Ser, pero ni falta que le hace. Si alguien sabe lo que piensa el presidente del Gobierno, es él. Sánchez ha empleado un tono bajo y defensivo con la crisis de Ceuta, pero ha afilado el cuchillo a la hora de hablar del ático de 400 metros que la Comunidad de Madrid compró por 6,3 millones de euros para que lo usara Isabel Díaz Ayuso. López, un tipo alto, de gafas cuadradas y bromista, se mueve en las mismas coordenadas que su jefe. Como ministro ha vivido un verano complicado por el colapso de la ciudad autónoma por la entrada masiva de inmigrantes; sin embargo, su candidatura del año que viene por el PSOE para gobernar Madrid ha recibido un impulso inesperado por la extraña operación inmobiliaria de su contrincante, que la tiene en fuera de jueg o y sin capacidad de reacción. Tras días de especulaciones, por fin la Casa Blanca dio más detalles sobre el histórico acuerdo por el que va a tener acceso privilegiado durante un siglo a una cuarta parte de las reservas de crudo de Venezuela . items.title: IT minister showcases digital transformation in Riyadh
items.description: IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja meets Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi, president of the Saudi Data and AI Authority.—APP • Shaza Fatima Khawaja stresses innovation, strong institutions and private-sector leadership as key drivers of digital growth • Calls for execution of measurable KPIs for successful transformation ISLAMABAD: Federal Minis­ter for Information Technology and Telecom­munication Shaza Fatima Khawaja said that Pakis­tan was now developing a na­­tional digital stack, which, combined with its young workforce, political and economic stability, and expanding digital infrastr­u­cture, would help accelerate the country’s digital transformation. “These steps have positioned the country as one of the region’s most attractive investment destinations,” the minister said while delivering a keynote address at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. Speaking at the session, “How We Built a Digital Nation,” she also formally inaugurated the Tech Des­tination Pakistan Pavilion and highlighted Pakis­tan’s digital transformation journey. She affirmed that the go­­ver­n­ment’s approach to gro­­­wth rem­a­ined ancho­red in innovation, par­tnerships, and smart investment. Pakistan had anchored its digital transformation in legislation through the Digital Nation Pakistan Act, which established the National Digital Commis­sion and Pakistan Digital Authority to ensure institutional ownership. She fu­­rther stated that the le­­gal foundation had been complemented by investments in connectivity and competitiveness, including one of the largest spectrum (5G) auctions , the creation of special technology zones, and reduced taxation for the IT industry. Sharing insights from Pakistan’s digital journey, the minister noted that the government had succeeded by leading through sound policymaking and strong institutions, there­­by creating an enabling environment in which the private sector can take the lead in driving growth. She emphasised that a dedicated central digital agency was essential to translating policy into effective execution, while discipline and measurable key performance indicators (KPIs) kept large-scale digital transformation focused and on track. The minister further un­­derscored that the state’s role lies in building core digital infrastructure that empowers the private sector to innovate and build upon it, noting that genuine digital progress is achi­eved through partnerships. She reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to further deepen its partnership with Saudi Arabia, expressing confidence that continued collaboration in digital innovation, capacity building, and emerging technologies would open new avenues for shared growth and prosperity for both nations. Earlier in the day, she formally inaugurated the Tech Destination Pakistan Pavilion, which featured 25 startups and 50 leading Pakistani technology companies showcasing inno­vative solutions in AI, automation, and digital technologies. Pakistan’s participation in LEAP 2026 aims to facilitate B2B partnerships, attract international investment, expand glo­bal market access for country’s technology sector, streng­then international business net­works, and create new opportunities for technology exports. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

Aaqib Javed defends Pakistan’s mid-series shake-up, says team failed to compete in England
items.description: KARACHI: National selector Aaqib Javed on Tuesday defended the Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) controversial mid-series shake-up , saying the team’s inability to compete in the first two Tests against England had forced the selectors to change the combination and “mindset” for the final match of the series. The PCB’s decision to sack red-ball head coach Sarfraz Ahmed — to replace him with white-ball head coach Mike Hesson — send seven players home and replace bowling coach Umar Gul with Australian Ashley Noffke has attracted widespread criticism, with former players and coaches questioning the wisdom of making sweeping changes with a Test still remaining in the series. Selection committee member Misbah-ul-Haq subsequently resigned after reportedly not being consulted over the changes. Speaking on a private news channel after the developments, Aaqib acknowledged that the selectors would have to take responsibility for the 17-member squad they had originally chosen but argued that the team’s management had failed to make the required decisions during the tour. “When we select a team, we sit with the coach and captain and build a squad. We are absolutely prepared to take responsibility for that squad,” Aaqib said. “But when you go on tour, you have to make the kind of combination you need from match to match.” Pakistan have lost both Tests against England, by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley and by 194 runs at Lord’s, leaving them 2-0 down in the series. Aaqib said the selectors had identified options within the touring squad, including an all-rounder, a second wicket-keeper and fast bowler Ubaid Shah, but those options were not used. “I also spoke to the captain and the coach before this Test match and told them to play your fast bowler, Ubaid Shah, because you have played three fast bowlers of essentially the same type,” he said. He also pointed to the lack of bowling options among Pakistan’s top seven batters as a reason for considering an all-rounder. According to Aaqib, the inclusion of a bowler such as Ubaid, who can shoulder a significant workload, would have changed the balance of the attack. “When you include a fast bowler like that, your entire bowling composition changes,” he said. The selector also defended the decision to alter the wicket-keeping arrangement, saying Ghazi Ghori, who was part of the touring squad, could have been considered in place of Mohammad Rizwan. Aaqib’s comments appeared aimed at drawing a distinction between the selectors’ responsibility for picking the squad and the management’s responsibility for deploying it effectively. However, he acknowledged that the selectors could not escape responsibility altogether. “The 17-member squad… I don’t think anyone had any doubts that there was something wrong with the players’ performances or that there was some deficiency in the squad,” he said. “But when you have played two Test matches in the West Indies (in July-August), and after those two Tests you are out of form, you are simply not performing and you are not even able to compete, then we have to do something.” The argument provides the PCB with a rationale for making changes before the Birmingham Test on Sept 9, despite criticism that the players and coaches should have been allowed to complete the tour before accountability was sought. Aaqib said Pakistan’s poor performances had made a change in approach necessary. “Now that you have lost the series, having lost both Test matches, there is no harm in changing your mindset for the third Test,” he said. “You can show the world that we still have talent.” He also defended the selectors’ decision to appoint Babar Azam as captain, despite the batter having previously been removed from the leadership position. Aaqib said Pakistan had few players capable of taking on a leadership role and that Babar, being a senior player and the team’s leading batter, was therefore considered the logical choice. He suggested, however, that the leadership and management had to be held accountable when performances failed to improve. “If you do not bring about any changes within it, then the problem becomes that the same players keep playing but do not perform,” he said. Aaqib also sought to explain the PCB’s decision to bring in Hesson, saying the New Zealander was familiar with the players and could get a better response from them. Hesson has been handed charge of the red-ball side for the final Test following Sarfraz’s removal. Aaqib said the message to the players was that performances and effort had to improve on important tours. “When you go on tour and play a series like this, you have to raise your performance, you have to compete, and you have to perform in important tours. There has to be a visible effort from the team,” he said. The selector also revealed that the PCB would initiate an inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq’s failure to bat in either innings of the Lord’s Test after suffering what was described as a low-grade calf injury. Imam was among the seven players sent home from England, along with Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Mohammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad. Five uncapped players have been drafted into the squad for the Birmingham Test. The wholesale changes have nevertheless raised questions about the PCB’s planning, particularly because five of the seven players sent home did not feature in the opening Test. Aaqib acknowledged the apparent contradiction but maintained that a failure to compete had left the selectors with little choice. He said the decision should be judged by whether the revised side could produce a better performance. “If this inclusion results in your team performing better, then surely that can only improve your image. What could possibly be worse?” he said. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

Xi visits Egypt as US sanctions threat looms over Iran links
items.description: BEIJING: Chinese Pres­ident Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday evening, making a rare trip to the Middle East as both countries face the threat of US sanctions over financial links to Iran. The months-long Middle East war, which began when the United States and Israel jointly launched strikes against Iran on February 28, has thrown the crucial trade region into crisis. Washington vowed last month to destabilise Teh­ran economically, warning of expanded sanctions against Tehran’s backers and partners that could hit Egyptian and Chinese banks, among others. Xi’s visit “comes at a time when China’s economic interests are directly exposed to the US-Iran war”, said Gamal Salama, political science professor at Egypt’s Suez University. China is “clearly seeking Egypt’s cooperation in managing and shaping regi­o­nal affairs”, said Liu Jia, a research fellow at the Singapore-based Mid­dle East Institute. Beijing works closely with regional actors such as Egypt, which mediates bet­ween Israel and Palestinian groups, Liu added. Both China and Egypt support an independent Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution. US threat to Egypt As part of its economic pressure campaign targeting Iran, Washington last week said it would cut off the operations of Egypt’s Ban­que Misr in the UAE from the US financial system. China, in response to the US threats, has vowed to safeguard its interests. The Chinese and Egyp­tian militaries carried out joint air combat exercises in August that featured J-16 fighter jets. Xi’s meeting with his Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, scheduled for Wednesday, follows a visit to Beijing by Jordan’s King Abdullah II, whose country has also been caught up in the US war with Iran. Xi told Abdullah in Aug­ust China “believes the sov­e­reignty and security of regional countries”. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

items.description: BISHKEK: The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The decision was anno­unced at the 26th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State in the Kyr­gyz capital, which was att­e­nded by PM Shehbaz Sharif. The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the pro­minence of a city that emb­odies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation. This year, Pakistan assumed the SCO presidency, with PM Shehbaz defining the theme of the chairmanship as ‘Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity’. Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26). The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek. The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

items.title: Govt told to renegotiate IMF terms
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan will phase out Export Processing Zones (EPZs) and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) nationwide by 2035, under the IMF’s Extended Fund Facility conditionality, to bring all sectors under a uniform tax regime, a parliamentary committee was told on Tuesday. The subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue directed the government to renegotiate with the IMF to prevent the potential closure of EPZs and SEZs, stressing the need to safeguard Pakistan’s industrial and investment interests. Talha Mahmood convened the meeting, which was attended by Dr Afnan Ullah Khan, Bilal Khan and Jam Saifullah Khan. The Ministry of Industries and Production briefed the committee on issues concerning EPZs and SEZs. After detailed deliberations, the convenor recommended that EPZs and SEZs should not be adversely affected and called for renegotiation of the matter with the IMF. Senate panel warns phasing out EPZ and SEZ will hurt exports The subcommittee also discussed difficulties being faced by exporters and businesses in banking transactions and emphasised the need for practical alternatives, including the use of insurance guarantees in place of bank guarantees or cheques, where permissible. The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) assured the subcommittee that the matter would be examined and resolved. The committee recommended introducing facial recognition technology to facilitate taxpayers whose fingerprints have faded or cannot be verified. FBR and NADRA were directed to coordinate and urgently resolve the issue. It was further directed that a list of FBR officials holding dual nationality and permanent foreign residency be submitted. The committee was also briefed on the National Auto Policy, particularly measures to promote the production and use of electric vehicles (EVs). It was apprised that viability gap funding is available to support the initial establishment of 3,000 EV charging stations nationwide. It was noted that early market closures affect businesses, particularly in the wake of power outages. The committee was informed that the current power situation was linked to disruptions in RLNG consignments and subsequent load-management measures aimed at keeping electricity prices lower. The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) briefed the subcommittee on unauthorised and illegal share transfers and legal disputes arising from forged signatures and other unlawful practices. The committee was informed that SECP has undertaken digitalisation of the share market and is taking strict action against individuals and companies involved in illegal activities. The committee stressed the need for FBR to strengthen its engagement with the business community by providing maximum facilitation and improving the ease of doing business. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

items.title: Humilité, dignité et persévérance : le Premier ministre célèbre l’exemple de Bénéwendé
items.description: À la clôture de la 2ᵉ édition de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO), le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a invité la jeunesse burkinabè à cultiver l’humilité, à rechercher constamment la connaissance, à préserver sa dignité et, surtout, à refuser les raccourcis et le chemin de la facilité. Ces valeurs trouvent une illustration concrète dans le parcours de la jeune Bénéwendé, une étudiante rencontrée fortuitement par le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, derrière son fourneau, alors qu’elle vendait du maïs grillé au bord de la route. Derrière le fourneau se trouvait en effet une étudiante en troisième année, qui exerçait cette activité pour disposer d’une source de revenus afin de subvenir à ses besoins. Cette attitude a retenu l’attention du Premier ministre. Non pas seulement parce qu’une étudiante vendait du maïs grillé, mais parce que son choix traduisait, dans la simplicité du quotidien, un état d’esprit : travailler, apprendre, persévérer et préserver sa dignité sans céder à la facilité. Ce mardi 1er septembre 2026, le Chef du Gouvernement a décidé de poser un geste symbolique pour encourager la jeune Bénéwendé : lui offrir une moto afin de faciliter ses déplacements, notamment entre son domicile et l’université, et de lui permettre de poursuivre ses études dans de meilleures conditions. Un geste dont il a lui-même précisé le sens : il ne s’agit pas de récompenser, mais d’encourager l’effort et l’exemplarité. « Tu incarnes ces trois valeurs » chères au camarade président du Faso, lui a expliqué le Premier ministre, en évoquant l’humilité, la soif de connaissance et le refus de la facilité. Il l’a invitée à conserver cet état d’esprit aussi bien à l’université que dans sa famille, convaincu que cette disposition d’esprit et cette culture du travail constituent un solide chemin vers la réussite. Étudiante en sciences de la vie et de la Terre (SVT), Bénéwendé nourrit l’ambition de se spécialiser en géologie. Pour elle, cette moto constitue non seulement un moyen de déplacement, mais également une motivation supplémentaire pour poursuivre ses efforts. À travers cette jeune étudiante, c’est bien plus qu’un parcours individuel que les autorités entendent mettre en lumière. C’est une certaine idée de la jeunesse burkinabè qui est célébrée : une jeunesse qui apprend, qui travaille, qui entreprend avec les moyens dont elle dispose, qui ne méprise aucun travail honnête et qui refuse de faire de la facilité un projet de vie. L’exemple mérite de faire tache d’huile. Car partout au Burkina Faso, dans les universités, les ateliers, les champs, les marchés, les entreprises et les quartiers, de nombreux jeunes consentent quotidiennement des efforts semblables, souvent loin des regards. Ils étudient tout en travaillant, entreprennent avec peu de moyens, soutiennent leurs familles et construisent patiemment leur avenir. Le message qui se dégage de cette rencontre est alors limpide : l’effort honnête n’est jamais insignifiant et le travail digne n’est jamais dévalorisant. En mettant en lumière de tels modèles, l’enjeu est moins de célébrer une personne que de faire grandir une culture collective de l’effort, du mérite et de la responsabilité. Et à travers l’encouragement adressé à Bénéwendé, c’est aussi un message qui est envoyé à tous ceux qui, souvent dans l’anonymat, font chaque jour le choix difficile mais fécond du travail et de la dignité : vous êtes sur le bon chemin ; persévérez ! DCRP/Primature L’article Humilité, dignité et persévérance : le Premier ministre célèbre l’exemple de Bénéwendé est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Anomalies dans les concours de l’ex-ENAREF cycle C et de la santé : Le gouvernement s’explique et annonce des sanctions disciplinaires contre les mis en cause
items.description: À la suite d’inquiétudes formulées par des candidats concernant le concours direct de recrutement de l'Institut des Finances Publiques du Burkina (ex-ENAREF), le ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple a officiellement reconnu des anomalies dans la prise en charge des copies d'examen du centre de Koudougou. Afin de garantir l'égalité des chances, les autorités administratives ont procédé à la correction immédiate des copies omises et à la réintégration des candidats nouvellement admissibles. Face aux doutes exprimés sur la crédibilité de la session 2026, une enquête interne a été ouverte pour identifier les responsables de ces dysfonctionnements et engager des poursuites disciplinaires. Le processus de recrutement de la fonction publique burkinabè traverse une zone de turbulences réglementaires. Des préoccupations émises par plusieurs candidats concernant le concours direct de recrutement de 184 élèves du cycle C de l'Institut des Finances Publiques du Burkina (ex-ENAREF) pour la session 2026 ont déclenché des vérifications approfondies. Les candidats s'inquiétaient d'une éventuelle mise à l'écart des enveloppes de copies provenant du centre de composition de Koudougou. Les contrôles internes diligentés par le ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple ont confirmé la matérialité des faits, révélant une prise en charge seulement partielle des copies de ce centre d'examen. Une anomalie qui touche également le secteur de la santé L'examen minutieux des procédures ne s'est pas arrêté à cette seule filière. Les investigations ont mis en évidence un problème similaire de prise en compte partielle des copies lors du concours direct de recrutement de 53 élèves Gestionnaires des services de santé. Face à ce double manquement administratif, qui touche des secteurs clés de l'administration et de la santé publique, le ministère a dû prendre des mesures d'urgence pour restaurer le principe fondamental de l'équité républicaine. La reprise des délibérations et l'intégration des admissibles Afin de préserver l'égalité des chances de l'ensemble des candidats, l'administration a immédiatement ordonné la correction des copies initialement écartées. Les résultats des délibérations des concours concernés ont été révisés, permettant l’intégration des candidats nouvellement déclarés admissibles au sein de la liste initialement publiée. Cette situation a suscité de vives réactions au sein de l'opinion publique et parmi les internautes, soulevant des interrogations légitimes sur la fiabilité de l'organisation générale des examens de la session 2026. Des mesures disciplinaires annoncées Dans un communiqué officiel, le Secrétaire général du ministère, Suanyaba Rodrigue Oboulbiga, a exprimé les regrets de l'institution face à ces incidents. Il a précisé que des investigations étaient actuellement en cours afin de situer précisément les responsabilités individuelles des acteurs impliqués dans ces manquements. Des mesures disciplinaires adaptées seront engagées contre les personnes mises en cause. Pour rassurer les candidats et l'opinion publique, le Secrétariat général a toutefois souligné qu'à ce jour, l'ensemble des copies scannées pour les 155 concours directs de la session ont été intégralement comptabilisées et corrigées, écartant ainsi le risque d'autres omissions systématiques sur le reste des épreuves. L’article Anomalies dans les concours de l'ex-ENAREF cycle C et de la santé : Le gouvernement s'explique et annonce des sanctions disciplinaires contre les mis en cause est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Pakistan launches dual-tranche Eurobond offering
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Tuesday launched the process for a US dollar-denominated benchmark dual-tranche Eurobond offering with five-year and 10-year tenors, as the government seeks to deepen its return to international capital markets following recent sovereign rating upgrades. Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad said in a post on X that the proposed transaction was subject to market conditions and represented another step in Pakistan’s renewed access to international capital markets. The size of the proposed issuance, pricing and final yields are yet to be announced and will depend on investor demand and prevailing market conditions. Mr Schehzad said the transaction followed improvements in Pakistan’s sovereign credit ratings and macroeconomic indicators and reflected the country’s growing engagement with international investors. The latest move comes less than five months after Pakistan returned to the international bond market following a four-year absence. Minister’s aide calls it another step in country’s renewed access to global capital markets In April, the government initially raised $500 million through a three-year Eurobond under its Global Medium-Term Note (GMTN) Programme at a coupon of 6.975pc. The issue was subsequently increased to $750m through a $250m green-shoe option after stronger-than-expected investor demand. The bond matures in April 2029. Pakistan has also repaid a $1.4 billion Eurobond that matured in April, allowing the government to re-establish a pricing benchmark in international debt markets after several years of relying heavily on multilateral, bilateral and commercial financing. On Tuesday, S&P also assigned a ‘B’ rating to Pakistan’s GMTN programme and the proposed benchmark US dollar notes, in line with the sovereign rating. Fitch Ratings also assigned the GMTN programme a ‘B-’ rating with a Recovery Rating of ‘RR4’, in line with the country’s long-term sovereign rating. The latest offering extends the maturity profile beyond the three-year tenor used in April, with the proposed five- and 10-year tranches providing a test of investors’ willingness to hold Pakistani sovereign debt for longer periods. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

items.title: « Donnez-moi les moyens et je construis la bombe atomique »: Les propos de l’Égyptologue Jean Magloire SOME enflamment la toile, … « Il faut faire la différance entre un plateau de télé et un kiosque » ….
items.description: Le passage de l’égyptologue et enseignant Jean Magloire Some sur le plateau de l'émission Surface de Vérité de la chaîne BF1 TV a déclenché une véritable tempête de réactions sur l’espace numérique burkinabè. En affirmant qu'il était capable de concevoir une bombe atomique « en un rien de temps » si l'État lui en octroyait les moyens, l'auteur du Codex grammatical égyptien a suscité un débat houleux. Entre ceux qui tournent ces déclarations en dérision, ceux qui réclament la présentation d’un devis chiffré et un arbitrage de la Présidence du Faso, et ceux qui dénoncent un manque chronique de confiance envers les cerveaux locaux, l'opinion se fracture en trois visions distinctes de l'ambition scientifique nationale. Le dimanche 30 août 2026, l'égyptologue Jean Magloire Some a prononcé une phrase qui résonne encore dans toutes les discussions de la capitale. Sur le plateau de BF1 TV, il a surpris tout le monde avec une phrase simple : « Je suis professeur d’anglais, mais donnez-moi les moyens et je construis la bombe atomique en un rien de temps » . Pour lui, fabriquer cette arme n'est pas si difficile. C'est juste une question d'atomes, d'oxygène, d'hydrogène et de contrôle des températures. Il affirme que ces connaissances scientifiques appartenaient déjà aux anciennes civilisations africaines avant d'être bloquées par l'esclavage et la colonisation. Cette déclaration a déclenché de très nombreux commentaires sur Internet. https://netafrique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AQMSVcmFB1guBWcTEfa_AYHev1PvMJz8g2PI744ncVqvbYDGUbMANFkSyvtGLLH63TBPfzGyKM_88wgc9l2vxkBLqRQR-bpOvQhTxaFB4KCJ5w.mp4 Pour de nombreux internautes, ces propos relèvent plutôt de la comédie ou d'un film hollywoodien. Certains se sont moqués de lui en usant de la parenté à plaisanterie en disant que c'était sans doute l'effet du dolo. D'autres ont plaisanté en rappelant que si Ouagadougou est la capitale du cinéma africain, ce n'est pas pour rien. C'est dans ce même registre de l'humour et de la blague que certains commentateurs ont réagi. Avec beaucoup d'esprit, des internautes se sont amusés à rappeler Jean Magloire Some, qu'il convient tout de même de ne pas confondre le sérieux d'un plateau de télévision avec les causeries décontractées d'un kiosque de quartier. D'autres critiques plus sérieuses se sont ajoutées sur le plan scientifique. Plusieurs personnes se demandent comment un enseignant d'anglais pourrait maîtriser la technologie nucléaire, alors que de grands pays n'y arrivent pas. Certains internautes rappellent que le Burkina Faso a déjà connu des annonces similaires qui n'ont rien donné de concret à ce jour, comme le projet de satellite du professeur Frédéric Ouattara ou les promesses de l'égyptologue Mamadou Dango. Pour tous ces sceptiques, cette histoire n'est que de l'illusion, ce qu'ils qualifie de « dôhi ». À l'opposé des moqueries, un autre groupe de citoyens préfère être pragmatique. Pour eux, au lieu de rejeter l'idée tout de suite, il faut aller aux faits. Le premier conseil donné à l'enseignant est donc très simple : « Qu'il fasse son devis ! » . Les gens veulent qu'il dépose un cahier des charges clair pour voir de quels matériels et de quel budget il a réellement besoin. https://netafrique.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AQNRAIjQuvqLyHU7U8-3cL3qPz2SLxmsy2zkeCcwmfCHRLvD8nlNwF9-1BzbWdVRlOB-OKDtrnniwy9AbMfoB4fN9IGhzcgO9JDk7_y45fEtcA.mp4 Ensuite, de nombreux commentaires demandent directement au président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, de lui donner l'occasion de traduire en réalité ses paroles. Des citoyens suggèrent que le gouvernement finance cette expérience pour en avoir le cœur net. L'idée générale est de le mettre à l'épreuve : s'il réussit, le pays obtiendra le respect du monde entier ; s'il échoue, le débat sera définitivement fermé et il devra en assumer les conséquences. Enfin, un grand nombre de personnes ont pris la défense de Jean Magloire Some. Elles critiquent vivement ceux qui rient de lui. Pour ces défenseurs, ces moqueries répétées sont la preuve d'un grand complexe d'infériorité. Ils expliquent que si ces mêmes propos avaient été tenus par une personne à la peau blanche, tout le monde l'aurait écoutée avec respect et sérieux au lieu de s'en moquer. Ces internautes rappellent que de grands inventeurs comme Thomas Edison n'avaient pas fait de longues études scientifiques avant de créer des merveilles comme l'ampoule électrique. Ils pensent que l'Afrique doit enfin commencer à croire en ses propres cerveaux et soutenir ses enfants pour avancer. Pour eux, refuser d'office d'écouter Jean Magloire Some montre simplement que les Africains n'ont pas assez confiance en eux. L’article « Donnez-moi les moyens et je construis la bombe atomique »: Les propos de l'Égyptologue Jean Magloire SOME enflamment la toile, … « Il faut faire la différance entre un plateau de télé et un kiosque » …. est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Iran hits back after US launches new strikes
items.description: Multiple explosions were heard on Tuesday evening across Iran's southern Hormozgan and southeastern Sistan and Baluchestan provinces, as US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the start of strikes against targets belonging to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Blasts were heard in the counties of Sirik, Bandar Abbas and Qeshm in Hormozgan, as well as Konarak and Chabahar in Sistan and Baluchestan, the semi-official Fars News Agency reported. The exact locations and origins of the blasts remain unknown, it added. Fars cited Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan's deputy governor for political and security affairs, as saying that at least five people, including a four-year-old child and a woman, were killed and over 50 others wounded in the US attack targeting the wedding ceremony in Sirik county. The semi-official Tasnim News Agency, citing local sources, reported six blasts in Konarak and eight south of Qeshm Island, with unofficial accounts suggesting an explosion from the island's airport. Meanwhile, Ali Khalilabadi, Sistan and Baluchestan's deputy governor for security and law enforcement affairs, said four projectiles hit Chabahar and Konarak, the semi-official Mehr News Agency reported. In a Tuesday post on social media platform X, CENTCOM said US forces have begun striking IRGC targets. "The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region." Tasnim also cited sources claiming that Iran had launched missiles toward US bases in regional countries, though the report has not been officially confirmed yet. Iran's main military command, Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said in a statement that in response to the US "air aggression," the Iranian armed forces will deal "crushing and shattering" blows to the United States. The latest strikes have further escalated tensions in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington and Tehran trading accusations and threats of further military action. IRGC claims beginning retaliation for US strikes The IRGC said on Tuesday night it has started strikes against US bases and assets in the region in retaliation for US attacks. In a statement published on its official news outlet Sepah News, the IRGC said its "regret-inducing response against the aggressors" have begun, noting its air defense had shot down a "hostile" US MQ-9 Reaper drone. Its aerospace forces also launched ballistic missile and drone strikes on Camp Titin in Jordan and Shaikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, reportedly killing "a large number" of US troops and destroying several key facilities and combat helicopters. It stressed that the US strikes will only protract the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and make the Iranian armed forces more determined to "suppress the foreign forces interfering in the waterway." The IRGC said the attacks began after the United States bombed a number of civilian places in Iran's southern coasts "out of desperation" and in retaliation for the US "criminal" and deadly attack on a wedding ceremony in Hormozgan province. The Jordanian Armed Forces-Arab Army (JAF) said later that the country's air defense systems on Tuesday evening intercepted and destroyed 10 of 13 ballistic missiles that entered the country's airspace from Iran in the past hours. Three other missiles fell in remote areas away from population centers, with no casualties or loss of life reported, according to a JAF statement. Trump warns of 'much harder' action US President Donald Trump on Tuesday commented on the US military strikes on Iran as "large and powerful" in a Truth Social post, and warned that Iran would courtface even greater strikes if it retaliated. If Iran "retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level," Trump warned in a post on Truth Social. "But it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!" Trump threatened in the post. In a phone interview with Fox News, he claimed US forces destroyed "a lot of radar" in Iran's network, including systems Tehran attempted to rebuild. "This is a very big hit today. If it goes a third time, they're going to be totally wiped out as a country," Trump said. "The (USS) George Washington is loaded to the gills," he added. "We're loaded up." Trump said Gulf allies were notified ahead of the latest strikes, according to a Fox News report. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei on Tuesday rejected as a "lie" the US claim that its recent attack on Iran's Larak Island was carried out because Iranian forces were preparing to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Addressing a weekly press conference, Baghaei pointed to frequent US claims about Iran's intention to develop nuclear weapons, saying that Washington's pattern was to fabricate a "lie every time to justify its crime." Qatar says mediation efforts intensifying Qatar said on Tuesday that diplomatic efforts with its regional partners are intensifying to reach a swift solution to the Strait of Hormuz crisis, warning that leaving the issue unresolved would lead to further escalation. Speaking at the foreign ministry's weekly media briefing, ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said discussions remained underway with Qatar's mediation partners, including Oman and Pakistan, following a series of diplomatic visits and consultations in recent days. Al Ansari said that there was no "tangible result" yet to announce but that further outcomes of the discussions and visits would be disclosed in the coming days, adding that diplomatic efforts over the past several days had centered on resolving the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. He said that Qatar was working with its partners to ensure that the crisis ends through "a diplomatic resolution that guarantees that the strait is open." Such a solution should allow products from the region to reach global markets, guarantee regional security and address the aspirations of the region's peoples for prosperity and security, Al Ansari added. Iran condemns EU support for US economic operation Esmaeil Baghaei on Monday condemned the EU's support for a US economic operation against Iran, saying that Europe could no longer claim "strategic autonomy." Baghaei made the remarks in a post on the social media platform X in response to an EU statement issued on Monday at the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors meeting in Asheville, the United States. The EU said it "welcomes efforts (aimed) at ensuring that Iran ceases its destabilizing activities and engages in peace negotiations with good faith, also through additional economic pressure, including through the US-led Operation Economic Outcast." "Europe can no longer speak of 'strategic autonomy' while merely executing Washington's orders," Baghaei said. The EU called for continued diplomacy with Iran to ensure regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that it remained ready to take further measures and maintain pressure on Tehran together with the United States and other partners. On August 19, Trump announced what he called "the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country," warning that countries providing a lifeline to Iran would face "tremendous economic consequences." (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: Machettes, capuches et vols de téléphones : Un réseau de braqueurs sur des motos scooter provoque une psychose noctambules à Bobo-Dioulasso
items.description: NB: Image générée par IA Dans la capitale économique du Burkina Faso, certains quartiers font face à une recrudescence d'agressions ciblant les noctambules et les personnes isolées. Selon une enquête de terrain publiée par le média Ouest Info , des délinquants opérant par binômes sur des motos scooters et armés de machettes sèment l'inquiétude à Belle-Ville, Lafiabougou et Bobo 2010. Agissant à des heures tardives ou très matinales, ces agresseurs tiennent en respect leurs victimes pour s’emparer de leurs téléphones portables et de leurs clés de contact. Face à cette menace récurrente, la vigilance et la restriction des déplacements nocturnes se généralisent chez les habitants. À Bobo-Dioulasso, si les efforts de maillage territorial menés par les services de sécurité visent à contenir la criminalité urbaine, certains quartiers demeurent le théâtre d'actes de grand banditisme. Comme le rapporte le média en ligne Ouest Info , de nouveaux groupes de délinquants perturbent la quiétude de plusieurs secteurs de la ville. Le mode opératoire de ces agresseurs est pratiquement identique d'un cas à un autre. Opérant généralement en binômes sur des motos scooters, vêtus de capuches ou encagoulés, ils patrouillent à des heures indues à la recherche de cibles isolées dans des zones sombres ou mal éclairées. Armés de machettes, ils surgissent brusquement pour exiger sous la menace les téléphones portables de leurs victimes. Une fois le larcin commis, ils confisquent systématiquement les clés des engins pour couper court à toute tentative de poursuite ou d'alerte rapide des forces de l'ordre. Des agressions traumatisantes à Bobo 2010 et Belle-Ville Les témoignages recueillis illustrent la détresse de citoyens ordinaires confrontés à cette violence imprévue. Dans la nuit du 20 août 2026, vers 23 heures, Awa et Ali, deux étudiants, se trouvaient dans une zone d'ombre à Bobo 2010 lorsqu'ils ont été encerclés par quatre individus sur deux motos scooters. Menacés d'être agressés à la machette, ils ont dû céder leurs téléphones portables et les clés de leur moto. Quelques jours plus tard, à Belle-Ville, c'est Mathias, un gérant de kiosque, qui a échappé de peu à un sort identique aux alentours de 1 heure du matin. Barré par quatre malfrats armés alors qu'il rentrait chez lui, il a dû son salut au phare d’un véhicule approchant, faisant fuir ses assaillants. Une insécurité matinale à Lafiabougou La délinquance ne se limite pas au cœur de la nuit. Le 11 août 2026, Dramane Coulibaly, étudiant travaillant comme vigile à Lafiabougou, a été pris pour cible vers 6 heures du matin alors qu’il rentrait de son service. Un binôme à scooter lui a arraché son téléphone portable sous la menace d'une machette, le laissant impuissant et terrifié. L'enquête de Ouest Info révèle également que d'autres victimes, comme deux sœurs agressées récemment, préfèrent se murer dans le silence pour ne pas revivre ce traumatisme. Face à la similitude des armes, des engins et des accoutrements décrits, l’existence d’un réseau structuré et spécialisé est fortement suspectée. En attendant leur interpellation par les forces de sécurité, la méfiance s'est installée et les habitants adaptent désormais leurs habitudes en évitant les sorties nocturnes non essentielles. L’article Machettes, capuches et vols de téléphones : Un réseau de braqueurs sur des motos scooter provoque une psychose noctambules à Bobo-Dioulasso est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: The Guard That Won’t Be Changing
items.description: M any Democrats of a certain age took the same message from the party’s 2024 debacle: Voters are sick of the old guard and craving younger, more aggressive leaders. Better to retire on your own terms than suffer the fate of Joe Biden, forced to stand down from his reelection campaign after a public humiliation. Nancy Pelosi, the 86-year-old former speaker, announced her exit from the House, as did her longtime lieutenant, 87-year-old Steny Hoyer. Senators Dick Durbin (81) and Jeanne Shaheen (79) passed up reelection bids this year, and so, too, did two senators merely in their late 60s. Senator Ed Markey, 80, heeded no such warning, and evidently, he didn’t need to. The Massachusetts Democrat is one of just two current senators whose tenures in Congress date to the presidency of Gerald Ford. But tonight, the oldest Democratic senator on the ballot this year trounced his much younger primary opponent, Representative Seth Moulton. The AP called the race a half hour after polls closed, with Markey leading by nearly 50 points. In a race that pitted ideology against age, Massachusetts Democrats opted for a progressive stalwart who will be 86 at the end of another six-year term over a more moderate 47-year-old challenger. Moulton, an Iraq War veteran who is concluding his sixth term in the House, moved left to appeal to a statewide primary electorate. But he could not hope to outflank Markey, who won support from Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Instead, Moulton urged voters to embrace “a new generation of leadership” and argued that he could more effectively fight for liberal causes than an incumbent in the twilight of his career. Markey had already faced that kind of challenge before, and won . Six years ago, he handily defeated then-Representative Joe Kennedy III, a grandson of Robert F. Kennedy who contended that the incumbent, after so many decades in office, was no longer up to the task. Young progressives, unimpressed with what remained of the Kennedy aura and appreciative of Markey’s record championing the Green New Deal, rallied to Markey’s side. But that race preceded Biden’s flameout in 2024 and the reckoning over the Democratic Party’s gerontocracy . Some Massachusetts Democrats believed that Markey could be newly vulnerable, especially if a popular progressive such as Representative Ayanna Pressley, who is 52, decided to challenge him. Mary Anne Marsh, a longtime Democratic strategist in the state, told me that after seeing the reception Pressley received at a party convention last year, she became convinced that “if Ayanna runs, she wins.” But Pressley opted to run for reelection to the House, leaving Moulton to challenge Markey. Moulton has never lacked ambition—he led a failed bid to oust Pelosi as party leader in 2018 and waged a short-lived presidential campaign the following year—but he’s neither as progressive as Pressley nor as well liked. He built a reputation as a moderate in the House Democratic caucus, and after President Trump’s victory over Kamala Harris in 2024, Moulton angered many on the left by accusing his party of being “afraid” to say that transgender athletes should not play women’s sports. He has since offered a partial apology to the transgender community, but the line became fodder for Markey, who said that he’d thrown “trans kids under the bus.” The issue was emblematic of Moulton’s struggle to convince progressives in Massachusetts that he shared their values. “He’s tried to become a progressive, but he does it by defining progressive in a way that nobody believes,” Marsh said. “He tried to become something that he’s not.” The Massachusetts race was a rare Democratic primary this year in which U.S. policy toward Israel did not become a flash point, as both candidates criticized Benjamin Netanyahu’s government and opposed new military aid to Israel. (Moulton announced last year that he would return donations from AIPAC.) Both public polling and Markey’s internal surveys showed a closer race until earlier this summer, when the incumbent began to pull away. A Markey adviser told me that voters had not really tuned in to the campaign yet, and media attention was focused on higher-profile Democratic primaries elsewhere. Markey’s age also did not become a big factor, perhaps because the years since 2020 have been kinder to him than they were to Biden. His support reflected a frequently overlooked nuance in the debate over whether the party needs new leadership: Older progressive leaders, particularly the 84-year-old Sanders, remain popular. “There’s a difference between being old and being part of the old guard,” the Markey adviser, who was not authorized to speak publicly, said. “Younger voters love Ed Markey, younger voters love Bernie Sanders, younger voters love Elizabeth Warren, and I think that has a lot to do with the fact that they take younger voters seriously.” Moulton tried to align Markey with a Democratic establishment that he said has failed to deliver progressive wins. He frequently invoked the name of Senator Chuck Schumer, vowing to oppose the New Yorker if he seeks to remain the Democratic leader. And Moulton even accused Markey of having ties to the disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein, an attack that, according to Marsh, backfired so badly that it might have sealed Moulton’s defeat. (Markey denied any affiliation with Epstein.) In the end, Massachusetts Democrats preferred Markey’s progressivism over Moulton’s relative youth. Markey might have been helped by the fact that the stakes in this primary were not as high as they were elsewhere this year—and certainly much lower than when the party pushed Biden to withdraw in 2024. Massachusetts is not in danger of going Republican in November. Democratic voters wanted a trusted fighter to wage battle against Trump for the next two years and—they hope—for transformative progressive policies in the four years after that. They didn’t seem to care much that the fighter they chose happens to be 80 years old.

items.title: Import-export auto: Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou, le self-made-man burkinabè de l’automobile qui connecte le Golfe aux pistes africaines
items.description: Des gratte-ciels étincelants du Golfe aux pistes animées d'Afrique de l'Ouest, un homme d’affaires burkinabè réécrit les règles du négoce automobile international. À la tête de Mr Autoservice Import Export et d’Aboubakar Autoservice International, Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou, plus connu sous le pseudonyme de Mr Autoservice a transformé la mégapole de Dubaï en une plaque tournante stratégique. En connectant les géants industriels américain et chinois aux marchés africains par la force du numérique et de la logistique de terrain, ce visage de la diaspora trace les contours d'une réussite économique moderne et décomplexée. Dans le bourdonnement incessant de Dubaï, capitale mondiale du transit et des affaires, les opportunités ne dorment jamais. C'est dans ce décor de verre et d'acier que Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou a choisi de poser ses valises et de bâtir son rêve. Sous la marque prometteuse de « Mr Autoservice », cet entrepreneur audacieux originaire du Burkina Faso s’illustre comme un trait d'union entre les plus grands marchés de la planète et le continent africain. Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou, plus connu sous le pseudonyme de Mr Autoservice Son secret ? Avoir compris que le commerce de véhicules au XXIe siècle ne se limite plus aux frontières régionales, mais se joue à l’échelle globale. En établissant ses bases opérationnelles aux Émirats arabes unis, il a créé un véritable pont commercial capable d’aller chercher la qualité là où elle se trouve — aux États-Unis et en Chine — pour la livrer directement aux consommateurs africains. L'alliance chirurgicale de la logistique et du numérique Loin des méthodes traditionnelles de l'import-export, le modèle d’affaires développé par ses deux enseignes phares, Mr Autoservice Import Export et Aboubakar Autoservice International, repose sur une formule moderne et hybride. D'un côté, le travail de terrain, physique et rigoureux : l’inspection méticuleuse des véhicules auprès d’un réseau dense de concessionnaires mondiaux, la maîtrise des formalités douanières et l’organisation de la logistique maritime. De l'autre, la puissance technologique : une présence numérique ultra-active sur les réseaux sociaux. Grâce à des vitrines digitales interactives, Mr Autoservice permet à un acheteur situé à Ouagadougou, Lomé ou Bamako de commander, de suivre et de valider l'acquisition de son véhicule en temps réel. Cette digitalisation du commerce de détail de voitures vise à renforcer la transparence des transactions à distance, brisant la méfiance historique liée aux transactions à distance. La rigueur pour bousculer les géants Dans un secteur souvent marqué par l'opacité, Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou a fait de l'éthique sa plus belle carte de visite. La transparence documentaire et le respect scrupuleux des engagements sont les moteurs de sa croissance rapide. Cette trajectoire, qui inspire désormais plus d’un, a d'ailleurs trouvé un large écho auprès de médias d'envergure régionale tels que Burkina24 , Pouvoirs Magazine ou Ghana Media . Au-delà des chiffres de vente et des convois de conteneurs, le parcours de Mr Autoservice est la preuve vivante qu'avec de la méthode, de la vision et un ancrage solide au cœur des hubs mondiaux, la diaspora africaine ne se contente plus de participer au commerce international : elle le dirige. À propos de Mr Autoservice Mr Autoservice est le nom professionnel de Kaboré Abdoul Djalilou, entrepreneur burkinabè basé à Dubaï et actif dans le commerce automobile international, l’import-export et l’acheminement de véhicules vers différents marchés.
